nodes.label: adr-0001
nodes.summary: A Rust executable with a data-driven, read-only MCP surface over stdio

nodes.label: adr-0002
nodes.summary: A canonical capability registry, with MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI, the CLI and the reference as projections

nodes.label: adr-0003
nodes.summary: One shared MCP server per repository, peers, and clients that start it themselves

nodes.label: adr-0004
nodes.summary: One canonical declaration, composed modules, derived projections, and performance as evidence

nodes.label: adr-0005
nodes.summary: One projection plan over the canonical inputs, named owners for every truth, and the site as a view of the registry

nodes.label: adr-0006
nodes.summary: CI planned from one model of what affects what, gates as repository-owned scripts, and the site deployed from the run that verified it

nodes.label: adr-0007
nodes.summary: Skills are data under the layer's skills section, and every surface that shows one is a projection

nodes.label: adr-0008
nodes.summary: Use cases are executable canonical objects of the layer

nodes.label: adr-0009
nodes.summary: Prompt capture happens below the model, or is reported as unavailable

nodes.label: adr-0010
nodes.summary: Curated knowledge is one kind with a class, not a second store

nodes.label: adr-0011
nodes.summary: Every directory in the layer carries a contract

nodes.label: adr-0012
nodes.summary: The Cockpit is a sixth projection of the registry, not an application over it

nodes.label: adr-0013
nodes.summary: Every web surface is discovered from its producer, resolved once, and projected

nodes.label: adr-0014
nodes.summary: A closed session is a shared object of the layer, not a local note

nodes.label: adr-0015
nodes.summary: The episode boundary is drawn by the provider, not by the model

nodes.label: adr-0016
nodes.summary: The scenario is a body section, not a header field

nodes.label: adr-0017
nodes.summary: An episode that opens is handed what the last one left

nodes.label: adr-0018
nodes.summary: Operational moments are objects of the layer, not pages of the site

nodes.label: adr-0019
nodes.summary: Distribution is one model, and every surface that ships the tool is a projection of it

nodes.label: adr-0020
nodes.summary: The capability graph is composed, not centralised, and projected twice

nodes.label: adr-0021
nodes.summary: The branch-to-worktree topology is derived from git identity and enforced everywhere

nodes.label: adr-0022
nodes.summary: The UI standard is an audit over a discovered page set, and its failures are fixed at their shared source

nodes.label: adr-0023
nodes.summary: Product features are objects of the layer, and the landing page is a projection of them

nodes.label: adr-0024
nodes.summary: An orchestrator is a provider only at the bootstrap level, and its worktrees are scratch checkouts

nodes.label: adr-0025
nodes.summary: Presentation order is one total order owned by the crate, not a decision each surface makes

nodes.label: adr-0026
nodes.summary: A capability module's area is derived from the features that name it, not declared beside it

nodes.label: adr-0027
nodes.summary: A command is declared once and every surface is a projection of the command graph

nodes.label: adr-0028

nodes.label: ci-gated-project
nodes.summary: A project where CI decides what is acceptable

does_not_fit_when: Checks are advisory by policy and a red pipeline is routinely merged past
There is no CI, in which case the lifecycle commands still work but the last link of every chain is missing
fits_when: A completion claim should require verification that actually ran, with its exit code recorded
Public capability claims are expected to name their implementation and their test
The pipeline must fail when a declared rule stops being invoked
facts.summary: Integration is gated, and a claim about the code is expected to have a test and a pipeline behind it.

nodes.label: long-running-work
nodes.summary: Work that outlives the session doing it

does_not_fit_when: The work is a single sitting and nothing needs to be recalled afterwards
You want a knowledge base; this keeps operational state, not documentation
fits_when: Decisions need to be findable later by the task and commit that made them
Progress must be quotable without reading everything that led to it
Something unresolved should block acceptance until it is answered
facts.summary: A task spans days, several sessions, or several people, and the reasoning has to survive the gaps.

nodes.label: repository-opened-in-ai-clients
nodes.summary: A repository opened in AI clients, not only by people

does_not_fit_when: No AI client ever opens the repository; the shell tool alone supervises the work
You want the server to route work or refuse writes outside an announced scope; announcements are informational and the task record is the enforced form
fits_when: More than one AI client opens the repository, in one checkout or across sessions, and they should read one layer
The layer's objects are worth exposing as resources and tools rather than as files a client may or may not open
You want a client to be able to say what it is working on and see what the others said

nodes.label: repository-with-authored-governance
nodes.summary: A repository whose rules were written by people

does_not_fit_when: The repository wants a single generated instruction file and is happy to hand ownership over
There is no governance to supervise yet, in which case start with the shipped skeleton instead
fits_when: The authored text should stay authoritative and a generated section can sit inside it
Enforcement already exists as git hooks, including dispatchers over a hook.d directory
Rules are written down and nobody can currently prove which of them run
facts.summary: There is already a CLAUDE.md, an AGENTS.md or an equivalent that somebody wrote and others follow.

nodes.label: several-agents-one-repository
nodes.summary: Several workers in one repository at once

does_not_fit_when: One person works one repository at a time and nothing is ever handed over
Coordination is the point and you want a scheduler; this tool reports overlap, it does not resolve it
fits_when: Work is divided by paths and it matters that the division is checked rather than agreed
Sessions hand work to each other and the handover has to survive the branch moving
You need to know which checkout a task record belongs to
facts.summary: More than one agent or person is changing the same repository in the same period, in worktrees or in sequence.

nodes.label: knowledge-failure-is-recorded
nodes.summary: A policy switch that is off derives nothing and says so; a derivation that fails inside a provider hook is recorded as provider.event.failed and the hook still exits 0

facts.claim: A policy switch that is off derives nothing and says so; a derivation that fails inside a provider hook is recorded as provider.event.failed and the hook still exits 0

nodes.label: knowledge-integrity
nodes.summary: Every knowledge record is schema-valid with no unknown key, uniquely identified, evidenced when verified, resolves every reference it names, and carries no conversation; check, doctor and `majordomus knowledge check` refuse a record that is not

nodes.label: knowledge-promotion-is-an-act
nodes.summary: verified is written only by promote with evidence on stdin or by a person editing the file, never by the deriver; promotion moves the record to curated/ and rejection supersedes it with a reason, each leaving a ledger line

nodes.label: knowledge-served-on-every-surface
nodes.summary: The candidates awaiting review, one record by id with its references resolved, and the derivation status of the checkout are one declaration each and answer with the same content over the command line, HTTP and MCP

nodes.label: knowledge-writer-observed
nodes.summary: A repository in which episodes close and no knowledge derivation follows within the stale threshold is reported as a stopped writer by doctor and watch, and the finding clears when a derivation is written

nodes.label: landing-page-is-a-projection
nodes.summary: The website's homepage and feature pages name no feature, module, command, provider or count of their own, and a stale product dataset is refused by the pre-commit hook and by the rust gate before it can be merged

nodes.label: ledger-integrity
nodes.summary: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event, and a malformed line is a failure rather than a skipped record

facts.claim: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event, and a malformed line is a failure rather than a skipped record
facts.note: The reader skips a bad line rather than crashing, and check, doctor and watch all report it. The ledger is the one durable record nothing else can reconstruct.

nodes.label: legacy-migration
nodes.summary: A repository on the pre-.ai layout is migrated once, explicitly, with a previewed plan and a verified backup of its local state, and the command is idempotent afterwards

facts.claim: A repository on the pre-.ai layout is migrated once, explicitly, with a previewed plan and a verified backup of its local state, and the command is idempotent afterwards

nodes.label: live-scenario-evidence-is-local
nodes.summary: A live scenario is not selected by a bare usecase run, its evidence is written under the ignored local half, and it never raises a command to covered; an undischarged obligation is reported unmet, never failed

nodes.label: live-scenario-is-read-only
nodes.summary: A live scenario may only run commands share/commands.yaml declares read-only, names no setup, and asserts an obligation only where something owes one; every other shape is refused by usecase validate with exit 10

nodes.label: local-state-ignored
nodes.summary: Checkout-local state lives under .ai/local/, is ignored by git, and is absent on a fresh clone or worktree

facts.claim: Checkout-local state lives under .ai/local/, is ignored by git, and is absent on a fresh clone or worktree

nodes.label: mcp-client-always-served
nodes.summary: A client that starts the MCP server from a checkout whose executable is missing or stale is served by the installed release when it is of this tree's generation and told so, and is otherwise refused with exit 12 naming the explicit build; nothing is built

nodes.label: mcp-client-autostart
nodes.summary: An MCP client opened in the repository starts the server itself, through the client configurations at the root and bin/majordomus-mcp, without ever building the executable

facts.claim: An MCP client opened in the repository starts the server itself, through the client configurations at the root and bin/majordomus-mcp, without ever building the executable

nodes.label: mcp-data-driven
nodes.summary: What the MCP server serves is decided by the manifest, the declared source classes and each file's front matter, so an object added to the layer is served with no change to the executable

facts.claim: What the MCP server serves is decided by the manifest, the declared source classes and each file's front matter, so an object added to the layer is served with no change to the executable
facts.note: The add, remove and break sequence through the built binary is tests/external_extension.rs in the crate; the shell case proves the layer init writes is served, and that a rule added to it appears.

nodes.label: mcp-degraded-not-silent
nodes.summary: A file of the layer the MCP server cannot read is excluded with a diagnostic naming its path and the index says it is degraded, never silently smaller

facts.claim: A file of the layer the MCP server cannot read is excluded with a diagnostic naming its path and the index says it is degraded, never silently smaller
facts.note: Two files of one kind claiming one identity are both excluded and both named. --strict refuses to serve a degraded layer; --inspect exits 10 on one.

nodes.label: mcp-lease-lost
nodes.summary: A server whose lease was taken over says so on the endpoint every reader probes, refuses to take on a new client, and reports that what its health describes is another process; the sessions it already had continue and it ends with them

nodes.label: mcp-lease-resilience
nodes.summary: Nothing a client leaves behind locks another client out of the shared server; a corrupt, empty, stale or abandoned lease is taken over and named, a client that cannot share is served alone with the reason logged, and a signal removes the lease before the server dies

nodes.label: mcp-peers
nodes.summary: Every client attached to a checkout's server is a peer named by its own initialize, and majordomus_peers lists every worker of the repository - its own board and the board of every other checkout, each peer stamped with the worktree it is working in - while majordomus_announce tells the others what it is working on and which paths it expects to touch

nodes.label: mcp-shared-server
nodes.summary: One shared server serves a checkout: the first majordomus mcp binds loopback HTTP with Swagger UI and MCP over HTTP beside its stdio session and logs the URL, every later client of that checkout attaches to it, and it ends when the last client leaves

nodes.label: mcp-stdio-surface
nodes.summary: The Rust executable serves the repository's AI layer to an MCP client over stdio, with protocol frames alone on stdout

facts.claim: The Rust executable serves the repository's AI layer to an MCP client over stdio, with protocol frames alone on stdout

nodes.label: mcp-uri-resolution
nodes.summary: A majordomus:// URI resolves the same way through the MCP resource read, the majordomus_get tool and the HTTP object route, and majordomus://repository answers repository.info as a JSON document tagged builtin

nodes.label: mesh-claims-cross-runtime
nodes.summary: An exclusive claim made on one runtime excludes an overlapping claim on every linked runtime, and concurrent claims resolve to one named winner everywhere

facts.claim: An exclusive claim made on one runtime excludes an overlapping claim on every linked runtime, and concurrent claims resolve to one named winner everywhere

nodes.label: mesh-compaction-keeps-what-is-live
nodes.summary: Compacting the cooperation journal changes nothing live — a handover nobody has taken keeps its stream for a bounded retention, who took a handover and who answered a review stay with them, and a compacted runtime that beats again is fetched again whole

nodes.label: mesh-cooperation-links
nodes.summary: Two runtimes of one repository link only through a signed, replay-protected handshake that checks protocol, repository identity and trust, and every refusal is typed and visible

facts.claim: Two runtimes of one repository link only through a signed, replay-protected handshake that checks protocol, repository identity and trust, and every refusal is typed and visible

nodes.label: mesh-declared-is-held
nodes.summary: An enabled mesh declaration whose shared server did not activate the mesh is a failed `runtime` check of `mesh doctor` (exit 10) carrying the server's reason, and a `Mesh: DECLARED ENABLED BUT NOT ACTIVE` line in the session-start briefing — never a quiet off; and this repository's committed declaration is tracked, enabled, allowlists the fleet and names a hub

nodes.label: mesh-firewall-is-derived
nodes.summary: The inbound admissions a mesh declaration implies on a machine — the multicast group's port, the declared hub ports whose address is the machine's, the server's port beyond loopback — are derived from the declaration by `majordomus mesh firewall`, which names the host's firewall backend, the commands that admit them and the firewall's own verdict, exits 10 when a rule is observed missing or the kernel logged a drop toward those ports, and whose `apply` runs the commands only as root and never over HTTP or MCP; `mesh doctor` carries the same verdict as its `firewall` check

nodes.label: mesh-liveness-expiry
nodes.summary: A runtime that stops beating — crashed, killed or partitioned — expires on its peers within the declared expiry, its claims stop excluding, and its restart reconnects as the same runtime without a duplicate

nodes.label: mesh-network-acceptance
nodes.summary: Separate Linux nodes on a real network discover each other by multicast, link, share claims and handovers, and recover from a partition and a crash, in a lab CI runs

facts.claim: Separate Linux nodes on a real network discover each other by multicast, link, share claims and handovers, and recover from a partition and a crash, in a lab CI runs

nodes.label: mesh-observation-not-authority
nodes.summary: A discovered node gains no execution and no authorization from being heard; only signed traffic from a linked node may change mesh state, and trust labels records under an explicit policy that defaults to deny_unknown

nodes.label: mesh-off-by-default
nodes.summary: No mesh discovery socket opens until the repository commits an enabled mesh declaration, and a disabled or absent declaration is reported as the reason, not an error

facts.claim: No mesh discovery socket opens until the repository commits an enabled mesh declaration, and a disabled or absent declaration is reported as the reason, not an error

nodes.label: mesh-one-registry
nodes.summary: Every discovery observation converges into one bounded registry, deduplicated by node and runtime identity across sources, replay-protected per instance, and every surface projects that registry and holds no peers of its own

nodes.label: mesh-repository-isolation
nodes.summary: Runtimes serving different repositories never form a cooperative link, even when they discover each other

facts.claim: Runtimes serving different repositories never form a cooperative link, even when they discover each other

nodes.label: mesh-three-runtime-convergence
nodes.summary: Runtimes linked only through a relay converge on one state digest, each event held once, with no replication loop

facts.claim: Runtimes linked only through a relay converge on one state digest, each event held once, with no replication loop

nodes.label: minimum-context
nodes.summary: A profile declares which context a worker should load and no more

facts.claim: A profile declares which context a worker should load and no more

nodes.label: models-no-secret-fields
nodes.summary: The model catalogue reports whether a vendor's named credential variable is set and can carry no secret value — the schema has no field one could hide in

facts.claim: The model catalogue reports whether a vendor's named credential variable is set and can carry no secret value — the schema has no field one could hide in

nodes.label: models-one-declaration
nodes.summary: Vendors and models are declared once in share/models.yaml, and the CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and Cockpit render that one declaration with no model name of their own

facts.claim: Vendors and models are declared once in share/models.yaml, and the CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and Cockpit render that one declaration with no model name of their own

nodes.label: models-routing-explains-itself
nodes.summary: A routing decision names why the selected model was selected and, for every excluded model, the first check it failed — the same answer for the same question, with no hidden state

facts.claim: A routing decision names why the selected model was selected and, for every excluded model, the first check it failed — the same answer for the same question, with no hidden state

nodes.label: new-code-is-covered
nodes.summary: Every executable line, function and region a change adds or touches in the Rust crate must be covered by a test; a change that leaves new code uncovered is refused, and untouched legacy debt is left alone

nodes.label: no-counts-in-context
nodes.summary: A hardcoded count in the always-loaded file is a failure

facts.claim: A hardcoded count in the always-loaded file is a failure

nodes.label: no-network
nodes.summary: The shell tool performs no network call, evaluates no generated text and deletes nothing recursively; its one declared request is the loopback peer probe

facts.claim: The shell tool performs no network call, evaluates no generated text and deletes nothing recursively; its one declared request is the loopback peer probe

nodes.label: no-silent-overwrite
nodes.summary: A hand-edited instruction file is never silently overwritten

facts.claim: A hand-edited instruction file is never silently overwritten
facts.note: update refuses, offers a diff, and overwrites only under an explicit flag.

nodes.label: no-transcripts
nodes.summary: A handover is a state record, not a transcript - its required sections must be present and non-empty, a placeholder body is refused, and its identity is computed and refused when written into the body; a transcript pasted into a section is not detected

nodes.label: obligation-closure
nodes.summary: A task that declares obligations reaches the outcome completed only when each one has evidence recorded against it, and evidence taken over files that have since changed, or at a commit the branch has since left, no longer discharges anything

nodes.label: obligation-establishment
nodes.summary: An obligation whose fact the tool can hold is established live rather than recorded — a clean tree, a remote-tracking ref that reaches the head, a trunk that reaches it, a published site that serves it — and a hand-recorded line neither discharges it nor rescues it

nodes.label: observatory-draws-nothing-it-did-not-read
nodes.summary: The Observatory at /ui/observatory and /ui/kiosk shows a scene only when the capabilities it requires answered with something to draw, or, for a scene of the mesh where no mesh runs, when the repository carries a recording of it, which it labels a replay; a scene without either carries no model and states the source's reason, on a server and in the published snapshot alike

nodes.label: open-question-gate
nodes.summary: An unresolved question blocks acceptance, and an entry the gate cannot parse is a failure rather than a silent pass

facts.claim: An unresolved question blocks acceptance, and an entry the gate cannot parse is a failure rather than a silent pass
facts.note: A gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one, so check, doctor and watch all fail on a malformed entry.

nodes.label: openapi-inferred
nodes.summary: The OpenAPI document is inferred, the tags are the modules, the examples are the benchmark cases, the responses are the router's statuses by kind, the prose is the one text every projection shares, and the site's API reference is rendered from the committed document

nodes.label: overlap-report
nodes.summary: Overlap between parallel workers is computed on claimed paths in both containment directions

facts.claim: Overlap between parallel workers is computed on claimed paths in both containment directions
facts.note: Reported, never blocking. Work in progress is reported and never blocked.

nodes.label: personal-layer-changes-nothing-shared
nodes.summary: A layer installed with --personal is one person's own in a shared repository: it changes no tracked file, no .gitignore line and nothing git status shows, and the command that makes the claim verifies it

nodes.label: pointer-integrity
nodes.summary: Every repository-relative reference in the always-loaded file is proven to resolve

facts.claim: Every repository-relative reference in the always-loaded file is proven to resolve

nodes.label: policy-parse
nodes.summary: The canonical policy is parsed and rejected if it contains an unknown key

facts.claim: The canonical policy is parsed and rejected if it contains an unknown key
facts.note: A restricted YAML subset. Tabs, anchors, flow maps and multi-line scalars are refused rather than guessed at.

nodes.label: product-domains-derived
nodes.summary: The product is filed under a few domains declared once as files of the layer; a feature names exactly one, and every domain's members, interfaces, guarantees and use cases are derived from the features that name it, so a stable feature cannot be left out of the product map without the model refusing it

nodes.label: product-features-discovered
nodes.summary: A product feature is one file under the layer, discovered rather than registered, and answered by the command line, the HTTP API, the OpenAPI document, MCP, the derived graph, the capability matrix and the website's homepage and feature pages with nothing else changed

nodes.label: product-projection-public-safe
nodes.summary: The dataset the website is rendered from carries only fields an allow-list names, so a feature's prose, a machine path or a field nobody allowed cannot reach a published page

facts.claim: The dataset the website is rendered from carries only fields an allow-list names, so a feature's prose, a machine path or a field nobody allowed cannot reach a published page

nodes.label: product-references-resolve
nodes.summary: Every reference a feature makes resolves against the registry that owns it, and one that does not is an error naming the file, the key and the nearest candidate rather than a page linking to nothing

facts.claim: Every reference a feature makes resolves against the registry that owns it, and one that does not is an error naming the file, the key and the nearest candidate rather than a page linking to nothing

nodes.label: product-surfaces-derived
nodes.summary: Which interfaces a feature is exposed through, what stands behind it and what it answers are derived from the registries that own those facts, never authored, and a source file that writes one down is refused by its schema

nodes.label: profile-axes
nodes.summary: Capability class, reasoning effort, output verbosity, context and verification are five independent axes

facts.claim: Capability class, reasoning effort, output verbosity, context and verification are five independent axes
facts.note: The axes are validated and projected into the worker's instructions. Whether a worker honours them is not observable from outside the worker.

nodes.label: profile-validate
nodes.summary: Every profile is parsed, its unknown keys rejected, and the default profile proven to exist

facts.claim: Every profile is parsed, its unknown keys rejected, and the default profile proven to exist

nodes.label: project-schema
nodes.summary: Milestones and issues are canonical repository files, and a key nobody reads is an error

facts.claim: Milestones and issues are canonical repository files, and a key nobody reads is an error
facts.note: The same allowlist rule the policy and the profiles live under. The filename is the id; a record that disagrees with its own filename is refused rather than reconciled.

nodes.label: project-status-derived
nodes.summary: Issue and milestone status is derived from recorded facts and is stored nowhere

facts.claim: Issue and milestone status is derived from recorded facts and is stored nowhere

nodes.label: projected-record-edit-is-landable
nodes.summary: A pull request that edits a projected plan record is not refused because GitHub does not show the edit yet, and the trunk is refused for it once a declared window has passed

facts.claim: A pull request that edits a projected plan record is not refused because GitHub does not show the edit yet, and the trunk is refused for it once a declared window has passed

nodes.label: projection-fingerprint
nodes.summary: Every generated instruction file carries its own stamp, and a hand edit is detected

facts.claim: Every generated instruction file carries its own stamp, and a hand edit is detected

nodes.label: projection-generation
nodes.summary: Provider instruction files are generated from the one policy, deterministically

facts.claim: Provider instruction files are generated from the one policy, deterministically
facts.note: Running update twice leaves the byte-identical file. The test asserts the hash.

nodes.label: prompt-asset
nodes.summary: A repository-local prompt renders against a closed set of state tokens, and an unknown token is an error

facts.claim: A repository-local prompt renders against a closed set of state tokens, and an unknown token is an error
facts.note: No conditionals, loops, includes or shell. A prompt that silently renders a misspelled token as literal text is worse than one that refuses.

nodes.label: prompt-assets
nodes.summary: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and an unknown token is a failure

facts.claim: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and an unknown token is a failure
facts.note: Covers name and filename mismatch, an empty description, an unknown front-matter key, missing front matter, and a block token used inline.

nodes.label: prompt-capture
nodes.summary: A declared provider hook captures the person's raw prompts below the model, and doctor proves it by running it

facts.claim: A declared provider hook captures the person's raw prompts below the model, and doctor proves it by running it

nodes.label: prompt-continuity
nodes.summary: A captured prompt names the episode it belongs to or records that none could be resolved; the archive is private, bounded and free of credential material

facts.claim: A captured prompt names the episode it belongs to or records that none could be resolved; the archive is private, bounded and free of credential material

nodes.label: provider-capability-evidence
nodes.summary: What each provider can do about the session lifecycle, prompt capture, driving a browser beside this server and reporting what a session consumed is one declaration with a citation per cell, every surface projects it, and no provider the declaration names goes unreported

nodes.label: provider-projections-one-renderer
nodes.summary: The provider bootstraps the policy declares (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, ...) are a target of majordomus generate, rendered from the policy and the provider templates byte for byte as the shell tool renders them, and generate --check refuses a hand-edited or stale one in CI

nodes.label: published-translation-is-declared
nodes.summary: A page of the published site written in a reader's language is declared with that language and a reason, and is refused unless the page declares the same language itself

facts.claim: A page of the published site written in a reader's language is declared with that language and a reason, and is refused unless the page declares the same language itself

nodes.label: reasoning-survives-the-session
nodes.summary: A decision and its provenance survive the session: the next session finds them in its context and handover, reuses a standing conclusion instead of consulting again, and reopens it only on new evidence

facts.note: the scripted advisor of session B would hang if it were asked, so reuse is proven by the absence of a consultation.

nodes.label: reasoning-works-with-no-advisor
nodes.summary: Majordomus reasons, decides, implements and validates with no advisor at all: absent advisors are reported as ordinary state, material uncertainty gets a structured local review, and the conclusion claims no independent review

facts.note: the case builds its environment from nothing (env -i, a PATH holding git and node only, no credential), so it holds on a machine where every advisor is installed.

nodes.label: record-resolution
nodes.summary: The right prior record is resolved by worktree and branch, and an unrelated one is never offered

facts.claim: The right prior record is resolved by worktree and branch, and an unrelated one is never offered
facts.note: Same worktree and branch, else same branch, else nothing. Ties within one second are broken by ledger order. Absence is reported as absence.

nodes.label: record-retention
nodes.summary: Rotating the ledger archives the oldest lines and never deletes them

facts.claim: Rotating the ledger archives the oldest lines and never deletes them
facts.note: Refuses to overwrite an existing archive, and does nothing when the ledger is under its cap.

nodes.label: record-search
nodes.summary: Durable records are searchable literally, across kinds, without an index

facts.claim: Durable records are searchable literally, across kinds, without an index
facts.note: A fixed-string grep in authority order. No ranking, no embedding, no index that could fall out of step with the records it describes.

nodes.label: region-projection
nodes.summary: A projection can own only the region between its markers, leaving the rest of the file untouched

facts.claim: A projection can own only the region between its markers, leaving the rest of the file untouched
facts.note: How a repository that already has a hand-written CLAUDE.md adopts Majordomus. An edit outside the markers is never drift; an edit inside them is caught. Malformed markers are refused, not guessed at.

nodes.label: release-archive-shape
nodes.summary: A release archive carries every path once and carries nothing but files and directories

facts.claim: A release archive carries every path once and carries nothing but files and directories

nodes.label: release-is-complete-or-absent
nodes.summary: A release publishes an artifact for every supported target or it is not published

facts.claim: A release publishes an artifact for every supported target or it is not published
facts.note: The build matrix stops at the first failure, publication begins only when every build succeeded, and the recorder refuses to write a record missing a target the model marks supported.

nodes.label: release-prerelease-channel
nodes.summary: A tag with a pre-release part is published as a prerelease, recorded on the prerelease channel, and never resolved as the stable release, so an unpinned installer and a node that follows stable keep the highest stable version

nodes.label: reproduce-command
nodes.summary: Every finding carries the command that reproduces it

facts.claim: Every finding carries the command that reproduces it

nodes.label: retention-caps
nodes.summary: The append-only ledger and handover store have retention caps that are checked

facts.claim: The append-only ledger and handover store have retention caps that are checked

nodes.label: review-is-never-fabricated
nodes.summary: A session cannot claim review it did not get: a consultation must name an advisor its recorded plan selected, a conclusion's review is computed, and reasoning check and doctor refuse a forged record, provider coupling, a model credential in CI and a refused claim in a document

facts.note: a negative case: each defect is planted and must be named by reasoning check (exit 10) and by doctor.

nodes.label: roadmap-derived
nodes.summary: The roadmap is derived from milestone state, and no document may be a second authority for it

facts.claim: The roadmap is derived from milestone state, and no document may be a second authority for it

nodes.label: routing
nodes.summary: Routing recommendations will be derived from measured cost and outcome data

facts.claim: Routing recommendations will be derived from measured cost and outcome data
facts.note: Recommendations only. Majordomus does not invoke a model.

nodes.label: rule-exemption-carries-its-reason
nodes.summary: A rule that no program can express says so in its own front matter, with the reason, and is counted apart from every rule that has a gate

facts.claim: A rule that no program can express says so in its own front matter, with the reason, and is counted apart from every rule that has a gate

nodes.label: rule-proof-is-named-and-resolves
nodes.summary: Every rule names what proves it, and every path it names is in the tree

facts.claim: Every rule names what proves it, and every path it names is in the tree

nodes.label: rule-resolution
nodes.summary: The effective rule set is resolved as a dependency graph in a deterministic order, and a set that does not resolve is applied by nothing

facts.claim: The effective rule set is resolved as a dependency graph in a deterministic order, and a set that does not resolve is applied by nothing

nodes.label: rule-state-is-derived-from-what-ran
nodes.summary: A rule's proof state is derived from the tree and the ledger together, and a mechanism that refuses violations is never reported as a run that passed

facts.claim: A rule's proof state is derived from the tree and the ledger together, and a mechanism that refuses violations is never reported as a run that passed

nodes.label: runtime-adapters
nodes.summary: Opt-in runtime adapters will clamp read size, output size and fan-out from profile-derived limits

facts.claim: Opt-in runtime adapters will clamp read size, output size and fan-out from profile-derived limits
facts.note: The one implementation studied was rolled back within days because its limits were global constants rather than task-derived.

nodes.label: rust-binary-artifact
nodes.summary: The Rust executable the rust gate built is published as an artifact with its provenance, and every Rust case drives the executable MAJORDOMUS_BIN names instead of building one

facts.claim: The Rust executable the rust gate built is published as an artifact with its provenance, and every Rust case drives the executable MAJORDOMUS_BIN names instead of building one

nodes.label: rust-coverage-floor
nodes.summary: Coverage of the Rust crate is measured with test code out of the denominator, on every change that can affect the crate and on every push to master, and the build fails under the floor in scripts/rust-coverage-threshold or under the session/continuity domain's own floor in scripts/session-coverage-threshold

nodes.label: rust-evidence-gates
nodes.summary: Every gate the Rust executable must pass is one script, scripts/rust-check, and CI runs that script on every change that can reach the crate

facts.claim: Every gate the Rust executable must pass is one script, scripts/rust-check, and CI runs that script on every change that can reach the crate

nodes.label: rust-hot-path-benchmarks
nodes.summary: The paths of the Rust executable that scale with the repository carry criterion benchmarks that build on every push, and every executable capability declares its benchmark policy, required or waived for a typed reason

nodes.label: rustdoc-complete
nodes.summary: Every item the crate exports has its rustdoc page at the route derived from its path and kind, no item page exists without its item, and a module added to the crate becomes a required page with no list edited

nodes.label: rustdoc-composed-from-the-topology
nodes.summary: The site build composes every published static surface into its output at that surface's mount, read from the committed topology with no surface named by hand, and refuses, naming the producer, when a published surface's artifact is absent

nodes.label: rustdoc-discoverable
nodes.summary: The crate's rustdoc is a web surface at /rustdoc declared by discovery from the crate, present in the topology, its committed projection and the home page whether or not its producer has run, and a running server answers /rustdoc/ from the tree its producer wrote

nodes.label: rustdoc-published
nodes.summary: The crate's rustdoc is published at /rustdoc with the site, built from the commit the site names, and is never committed

facts.claim: The crate's rustdoc is published at /rustdoc with the site, built from the commit the site names, and is never committed

nodes.label: rustdoc-referenced
nodes.summary: Every builtin module's page on the site links the page the crate's reference documents that module on, from the one module-to-page mapping the rustdoc check holds the published tree to, and only in a build that composed the reference

nodes.label: rustdoc-verified-live
nodes.summary: A rustdoc tree built from another commit than the one it is checked or deployed as is refused, by the integrity check before publication and by the public verification after it

facts.claim: A rustdoc tree built from another commit than the one it is checked or deployed as is refused, by the integrity check before publication and by the public verification after it

nodes.label: schema-driven-kinds
nodes.summary: How each declarative kind is read and which keys it may carry is data read at run time, and a repository adds a kind with its JSON Schema without a code change

facts.claim: How each declarative kind is read and which keys it may carry is data read at run time, and a repository adds a kind with its JSON Schema without a code change

nodes.label: scope-declared
nodes.summary: What a worker reads of the repository is declared once in .ai/repo/scope.yaml, out wins over in, and the Rust executable discovers, indexes and serves nothing outside it

facts.claim: What a worker reads of the repository is declared once in .ai/repo/scope.yaml, out wins over in, and the Rust executable discovers, indexes and serves nothing outside it

nodes.label: scope-enforcement
nodes.summary: A touched file outside the claimed scope is a failure, not a warning

facts.claim: A touched file outside the claimed scope is a failure, not a warning

nodes.label: scoped-task
nodes.summary: A task is started with a declared file scope and a profile, and only one task is active per checkout

facts.claim: A task is started with a declared file scope and a profile, and only one task is active per checkout
facts.note: A scope path that escapes the repository root is refused. Starting a second task while one is active is refused.

nodes.label: semantic-retrieval
nodes.summary: Ranked or semantic retrieval over durable records is deliberately not implemented

facts.claim: Ranked or semantic retrieval over durable records is deliberately not implemented

nodes.label: session-lifecycle
nodes.summary: A provider hook opens the episode below the model and hands the worker what the last one left, records what a compaction is about to discard, and closes the episode with a continuation record beside its envelope

nodes.label: session-observability
nodes.summary: The session subsystem has a reading of itself — every open episode of the store and not only the one the pointer follows, the episodes that can no longer close themselves, the commit the serving process is answering about, and what each provider's adapter declares

nodes.label: session-records
nodes.summary: A closed execution episode is a shared object of the layer, written by the tool from git and the ledger, valid against a contract that admits no conversation and no absolute path, and discovered rather than registered

nodes.label: session-start-prompt
nodes.summary: A bare claude in a supervised repository starts with the repository's session-start prompt as its first message, and a run with an argument, outside such a repository, with the opt-out, or with a prompt that cannot be rendered is left exactly as it was

nodes.label: shared-policy
nodes.summary: One policy will be shared across repositories and workers

facts.claim: One policy will be shared across repositories and workers

nodes.label: site-deploy-one-path
nodes.summary: The site is deployed by one script, scripts/site-deploy, from a terminal or from the publication workflow; it refuses a dirty tree, a commit master does not contain and a build that is not HEAD's, pushes site/public to gh-pages with the source commit named, and pushes nothing when the output is unchanged

nodes.label: site-deploys-from-verified-run
nodes.summary: Publication is gated on everything that can make the published site wrong and waits for nothing else; the checks that decide whether a change may merge run beside it on the same commit, not in front of it

nodes.label: site-registry-dataset
nodes.summary: The site's Registry page is rendered from site/data/registry/registry.json, a dataset majordomus generate site derives from the registry and the index with their fingerprints, and generate --check refuses a stale one in CI

nodes.label: skill-catalogue
nodes.summary: A skill is one directory under the layer's skills section holding SKILL.md, discovered by the source class `skill` the shell tool and the Rust executable both read, so that adding the file is the whole registration and the catalogue, the command, doctor, MCP and the site all derive from it

nodes.label: skill-check
nodes.summary: Every skill is validated against the allow-list generated from its schema, its directory, its sections and its references, a violation names the file and every reason, and a repository with no skills is reported rather than passed

nodes.label: skill-site-projection
nodes.summary: The website's skills section is rendered from the skills catalogue, one page per skill carrying the skill's own body and examples, and a removed or renamed skill leaves no page, entry or link behind

facts.claim: The website's skills section is rendered from the skills catalogue, one page per skill carrying the skill's own body and examples, and a removed or renamed skill leaves no page, entry or link behind

nodes.label: suite-parallel
nodes.summary: The behavioural suite runs a bounded number of cases at a time with the serial runner's semantics, a case that writes into the checkout declares itself exclusive and runs alone, and the parallel phase fails naming the paths when the checkout changed under it

nodes.label: task-commit-attribution
nodes.summary: A task will know which commits it produced, rather than inferring them from a range

facts.claim: A task will know which commits it produced, rather than inferring them from a range

nodes.label: task-dependencies
nodes.summary: A task record has no dependencies; sequencing between sessions is not represented

facts.claim: A task record has no dependencies; sequencing between sessions is not represented

nodes.label: telemetry
nodes.summary: Execution telemetry will be recorded once a provider exposes it honestly

facts.claim: Execution telemetry will be recorded once a provider exposes it honestly
facts.note: Nothing measures token spend today. Any estimated_ field is labelled and excluded from enforcement.

nodes.label: the-closing-question-is-measured
nodes.summary: Whether a task added debt, left a branch or a worktree behind, or grew the backlog is answered by the done invariant from git, the debt baselines and the recorded forge observation, measured from where the task started; a reading that was not taken is unknown, never a pass

facts.note: the readings are the repository's, not one worker's; the case adds an entry to a baseline, creates a branch and a worktree, and breaks the task's starting commit to see unknown instead of pass.

nodes.label: token-savings-measured
nodes.summary: Majordomus will state a total-token change only from matched, verified runs that meet the methodology's publication rule

facts.claim: Majordomus will state a total-token change only from matched, verified runs that meet the methodology's publication rule
facts.note: The benchmark, its runner and its calculator exist; what is missing is enough evidence. The generated report states what the recorded runs show and why no claim follows yet.

nodes.label: tool-location-independent
nodes.summary: The tool runs read-only from any location, and two locations of one version agree about one repository

facts.claim: The tool runs read-only from any location, and two locations of one version agree about one repository

nodes.label: typed-outcome
nodes.summary: An outcome is a value from a closed vocabulary, not free text

facts.claim: An outcome is a value from a closed vocabulary, not free text
facts.note: no_match means the work was done and the thing sought does not exist. failed means the work could not be done. They are different facts.

nodes.label: ui-dashboard-cites-its-sources
nodes.summary: The UI's dashboard at /ui links every capability it read to that capability's page, serves under the Cockpit's security policy, and never waits for the pull-request queue, which is a page and a fragment of its own

nodes.label: use-case-coverage
nodes.summary: Every public command is named and run by an active use case, a guaranteed claim or an MCP tool without one is a named gap, and the policy says which gaps fail doctor, check and finish

facts.claim: Every public command is named and run by an active use case, a guaranteed claim or an MCP tool without one is a named gap, and the policy says which gaps fail doctor, check and finish

nodes.label: use-case-evidence
nodes.summary: A use case's scenario executes against the real tool in a disposable repository, every step's exit code and output are asserted, and the normalised evidence is what the site shows

facts.claim: A use case's scenario executes against the real tool in a disposable repository, every step's exit code and output are asserted, and the normalised evidence is what the site shows

nodes.label: use-case-impact
nodes.summary: From the files a change touched, the tool names the commands, rules, use cases, scenarios and behavioural cases affected, and scaffolds a draft for a capability no use case covers

facts.claim: From the files a change touched, the tool names the commands, rules, use cases, scenarios and behavioural cases affected, and scaffolds a draft for a capability no use case covers

nodes.label: vendored-rule-package
nodes.summary: The rule baseline is vendored into the repository with a manifest naming every file and its hash, and a hand edit is detected and refused

facts.claim: The rule baseline is vendored into the repository with a manifest naming every file and its hash, and a hand edit is detected and refused

nodes.label: web-namespaces-reserved
nodes.summary: /docs serves this repository's documentation and /swagger serves the Swagger UI, and neither may take the other's mount

facts.claim: /docs serves this repository's documentation and /swagger serves the Swagger UI, and neither may take the other's mount

nodes.label: web-surface-declared-once
nodes.summary: Every web surface is declared once at its producer and resolved into one topology, from which the router, the landing page and the machine-readable index are each projected

facts.claim: Every web surface is declared once at its producer and resolved into one topology, from which the router, the landing page and the machine-readable index are each projected

nodes.label: why-catalogue-discovered
nodes.summary: An operational moment is one file under the layer, discovered rather than registered, and answered by the command line, the HTTP API, the OpenAPI document, MCP, the derived graph and the website with nothing else changed

facts.note: Removing the file removes it from all of them, which is what a hidden registry would fail.

nodes.label: why-diagnosis-explainable
nodes.summary: A diagnosis of a reader's own symptoms is deterministic counting over the catalogue's metadata, and every recommendation names the moments that produced it

facts.claim: A diagnosis of a reader's own symptoms is deterministic counting over the catalogue's metadata, and every recommendation names the moments that produced it
facts.note: No weighting and no percentage; the questionnaire on the website and `majordomus why diagnose` run the same arithmetic over the same data.

nodes.label: why-references-resolve
nodes.summary: Every reference a moment makes resolves against the thing it names, and one that does not is an error carrying the nearest candidate

facts.claim: Every reference a moment makes resolves against the thing it names, and one that does not is an error carrying the nearest candidate
facts.note: Audiences, areas and related moments against the catalogue; commands, capabilities, claims, rules and use cases against their own registries.

nodes.label: wiring-reconciliation
nodes.summary: Every enforcement the policy declares is reconciled against what actually runs

facts.claim: Every enforcement the policy declares is reconciled against what actually runs
facts.note: The path must exist, be executable, and be invoked by the named dispatcher. A hook that invokes it and discards the exit code counts as not wired.

nodes.label: worktree-migration-lossless
nodes.summary: A misplaced worktree is brought to its canonical path with its modified, staged, unstaged and untracked work intact, verified by a fingerprint taken before and after the move, and a step is reported as moved only when the two are equal

nodes.label: worktree-ownership
nodes.summary: A task record names the checkout it belongs to, and another checkout is never held to its scope

facts.claim: A task record names the checkout it belongs to, and another checkout is never held to its scope

nodes.label: worktree-topology-derived
nodes.summary: A branch's worktree path is derived from git identity and the branch name alone — the primary checkout's sibling named with -wt, then the branch with its hierarchy kept — and is the same answer from every directory of every worktree, with nothing registered or configured

nodes.summary: adr

nodes.label: archive
nodes.summary: archive

facts.summary: Take a snapshot of the tracked tree that can be read, or checked, somewhere else.

nodes.label: bench

nodes.label: checkpoint

nodes.label: context
nodes.summary: context

facts.summary: What the next worker needs to know now, in authority order and within a budget.

nodes.summary: decision

nodes.summary: doctor

facts.summary: It checks governance only: is Majordomus itself healthy, and is every enforcement it declares actually wired here?

nodes.label: doctrine
nodes.summary: doctrine

facts.summary: What rules are enforced, by what, and whether each one is actually wired.

nodes.label: evidence
nodes.summary: evidence

nodes.label: finish
nodes.summary: finish

facts.note: --check evaluates without writing and exits 0 when no task is active, so a pre-push hook never blocks a repository with nothing to enforce.
facts.summary: Evaluate the finish contract and refuse the outcome if any line of it is unmet.

nodes.label: handover
nodes.summary: handover

facts.summary: Write an append-only continuation record, and resolve the most relevant prior one.

nodes.label: help
nodes.summary: help

facts.summary: Print the usage text, which is the list of every public command.

nodes.label: history
nodes.summary: history

facts.note: --validate reports malformed lines and exits 10. --rotate archives old lines and is the one subcommand that writes; it never deletes and refuses while under the cap.
facts.summary: Read the append-only ledger back, filtered by task, event or time.

nodes.label: init
nodes.summary: init

facts.summary: Create the .ai/ layer in this repository, and refuse to overwrite an existing one.

nodes.label: knowledge
nodes.summary: knowledge

facts.summary: The compiled index over what this repository states, and the candidate records it derives from what an episode did.

nodes.label: migrate
nodes.summary: migrate

facts.summary: Move pre-.ai project data from .majordomus/ into .ai/, explicitly and backed up.

nodes.label: plan
nodes.summary: plan

facts.summary: The milestone and issue model — validate it, read it, and move one issue through it.

nodes.label: prompt
nodes.summary: prompt

facts.note: An unknown token, or a block token used inline, is an error rather than a literal left in the output.
facts.summary: List, show and render the repository's own prompt assets, substituting known tokens only.

nodes.summary: question

facts.note: Every unresolved entry for the active task refuses finish --outcome completed. That is the whole point of the command; it is a gate, not a notebook.
facts.summary: Open a question that blocks acceptance, resolve it, and list what is still open.

nodes.label: recover
nodes.summary: recover

facts.summary: Close episodes nobody ended, fold duplicate records, classify the stores' stray files.

nodes.label: rules

facts.summary: Open, inspect and close one execution episode.

nodes.label: skills

facts.summary: The repository's skills — provider-neutral procedures under the skills section — listed, shown and checked from the one catalogue every surface reads.

nodes.label: start
nodes.summary: start

facts.summary: Begin one scoped task under a profile, and refuse while another is active.

nodes.label: update
nodes.summary: update

facts.summary: Regenerate every provider instruction file from the one policy, deterministically.

nodes.label: usecase
nodes.summary: usecase

facts.summary: The executable use cases: list, show, validate, run against the real tool, coverage, impact, scaffold.

nodes.label: version
nodes.summary: version

facts.note: The string every other surface derives its version from. It runs before anything is installed, which is why it is dispatched ahead of the option parser.
