nodes.label: docs/claims/a-candidate-is-routed-by-what-it-is-about.md
nodes.summary: Every observation candidate is routed by the structure of what it is about

nodes.label: docs/claims/a-diagram-is-named-linked-and-addressable.md
nodes.summary: Every Mermaid diagram of the built site gets an id (diagram-<name>), the list of its nodes, the viewer's controls and a link for each node that is the identity of an object the site has a page for, all derived at build; a link to #diagram-<name>:<node> fails the build when the diagram does not declare the node

nodes.label: docs/claims/a-finding-names-how-to-see-it-again.md
nodes.summary: Every finding a command reports names the command that reproduces it

nodes.label: docs/claims/a-session-records-what-it-observed.md
nodes.summary: knowledge observe records one observation.recorded line of a fixed shape, and refuses any other

nodes.label: docs/claims/a-skipped-case-is-not-a-proof.md
nodes.summary: A test case that declines to run is reported as a skip and recorded as one, so the evidence ledger can never read a case that asserted nothing as the proof of the claim it names

nodes.label: docs/claims/adr-catalogue.md
nodes.summary: An architecture decision is one file under the layer's adrs section, validated against the decision contract, with an identity nothing else claims, reciprocal supersession, and every reference it makes resolving

nodes.label: docs/claims/adr-propose.md
nodes.summary: `majordomus adr propose` writes a decision with status proposed and refuses to write any other status, allocates its identity under a lock so concurrent workers never collide, and records what the decision was derived from

nodes.label: docs/claims/adr-traceability.md
nodes.summary: A decision states what it put in force as typed references, each one validated, and the reverse direction is read from the knowledge graph rather than written down a second time

nodes.label: docs/claims/advertised-install-command-works.md
nodes.summary: The install command this project advertises is run, from the published site, and proved to work

nodes.label: docs/claims/advice-is-weighed-not-counted.md
nodes.summary: Advisors that disagree never decide by count: a conclusion is refused while a disagreement on its assessment is unsettled, a resolution needs evidence, and every answer received must be weighed

nodes.label: docs/claims/advisor-failure-is-recorded-and-recovers.md
nodes.summary: An advisor that times out, is rate limited, refuses its credential or answers malformed is recorded as exactly that, never blocks the work, opens a circuit that closes again after its cooldown, and never fails the session

nodes.label: docs/claims/advisor-transports-share-one-contract.md
nodes.summary: Every advisor transport is held to one contract — typed failures, deadlines, cancellation, normalised answers, reported usage, redacted secrets — proven against fakes with no network, model or credential

nodes.label: docs/claims/advisors-are-declared-once.md
nodes.summary: Advisors are declared once, in share/advisors.yaml, by reference to the provider table and the model catalogue; a new advisor reaches the command line, the policy, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and the Cockpit with no consumer edited

nodes.label: docs/claims/ai-layer-manifest.md
nodes.summary: The repository's AI layer is one directory whose manifest names every section, readable without the tool

nodes.label: docs/claims/an-observation-becomes-a-grouped-candidate.md
nodes.summary: Each observation becomes a candidate of its own at its episode's end, and reading groups them by subject

nodes.label: docs/claims/archive-fidelity.md
nodes.summary: An archive that lost the file modes fails rather than travelling

nodes.label: docs/claims/authored-files-are-english.md
nodes.summary: Every authored file in this repository is spelled in English

nodes.label: docs/claims/benchmark-coverage-derived.md
nodes.summary: Every externally callable operation of the Rust executable is a benchmark target with a denominator generated from the registry, and a missing case fails the structural check

nodes.label: docs/claims/blocker-store.md
nodes.summary: An unparseable question blocks acceptance exactly as an unresolved one does

nodes.label: docs/claims/blocker-survives-handover.md
nodes.summary: A blocking question keeps blocking after the work is handed to a new task

nodes.label: docs/claims/bootstrap-chain.md
nodes.summary: Provider instruction files are thin bootstraps that point at the AI layer and carry no rule of their own

nodes.label: docs/claims/briefing-names-candidates.md
nodes.summary: The start briefing names the candidates awaiting review on this branch, count and ids, bounded and within the briefing budget, and prints their absence rather than omitting it

nodes.label: docs/claims/candidates-reviewed-not-accumulated.md
nodes.summary: More candidates than the policy cap, or a candidate older than the policy age, is an advisory doctor finding that names them

nodes.label: docs/claims/capability-class.md
nodes.summary: A profile names a capability class rather than a vendor model

nodes.label: docs/claims/capability-modules.md
nodes.summary: A capability of the Rust executable is declared once and composed into its module, the root composes modules, and the registry refuses a capability outside its module's namespace

nodes.label: docs/claims/capability-registry.md
nodes.summary: Every capability of the Rust executable is defined once, and the registry refuses a duplicate id or a colliding projection name, naming both parties

nodes.label: docs/claims/catalogue-resolves.md
nodes.summary: A use case cannot name something the tool does not have

nodes.label: docs/claims/checkpoint-interval.md
nodes.summary: A profile sets how often a worker should checkpoint, and a stale task is reported

nodes.label: docs/claims/checkpoint-record.md
nodes.summary: A checkpoint is a capped progress record, and a body over the cap is refused

nodes.label: docs/claims/ci-planned-gates.md
nodes.summary: A change runs the gates its paths can affect, decided by one model of what affects what, and a change to the pipeline itself or a path the model does not know runs every gate

nodes.label: docs/claims/ci-verdict-is-required.md
nodes.summary: No pull request can be merged into the default branch while the verdict status is red, because a branch rule requires it

nodes.label: docs/claims/ci-verdict.md
nodes.summary: The verdict status is green only when planning succeeded and every gate the plan selected ran in a job that succeeded; a failed or cancelled job, a selected gate whose job was skipped, or a plan that selected nothing is red

nodes.label: docs/claims/cli-documentation-executable.md
nodes.summary: Every command of the Rust executable's command line carries a summary, help on every argument and, where it runs, at least one example, the root carries a long description, and every example shown to a reader is executed against the built executable

nodes.label: docs/claims/cockpit-is-a-projection-of-the-registry.md
nodes.summary: A capability added to the registry reaches every Cockpit surface without one line of the Cockpit being edited

nodes.label: docs/claims/command-coverage.md
nodes.summary: Every public command has a behavioural test and a negative test, computed rather than remembered

nodes.label: docs/claims/command-surface.md
nodes.summary: The public command surface is declared, and reconciled against the dispatcher

nodes.label: docs/claims/commit-message-is-judged.md
nodes.summary: A commit message that does not satisfy the policy is refused while it is being written

nodes.label: docs/claims/commit-plan-is-refusable.md
nodes.summary: A commit plan carries what it was derived from, so a stale one is refused rather than applied

nodes.label: docs/claims/commit-scopes-are-learned.md
nodes.summary: The scope vocabulary is learned from the history, not kept in a table

nodes.label: docs/claims/connection-episode.md
nodes.summary: A client with no provider hooks gets an execution episode from the MCP connection, resumes its own after a crash, and never has its prompt claimed to be captured

nodes.label: docs/claims/consistency-check.md
nodes.summary: check reports whether state, scope, blockers and checkpoint age are consistent right now

nodes.label: docs/claims/context-assembly.md
nodes.summary: The context a worker is given is assembled from durable state in authority order

nodes.label: docs/claims/context-budget.md
nodes.summary: The always-loaded instruction file has a line budget with a failing check

nodes.label: docs/claims/context-coverage.md
nodes.summary: Every directory of the layer carries a context document, the exemption is declared by the contract that governs the subtree, and a descendant may narrow that requirement but never weaken it

nodes.label: docs/claims/context-documents.md
nodes.summary: The context that applies to a path is composed from the layer's scoped documents, root to target, in one deterministic order with provenance, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing

nodes.label: docs/claims/context-impact.md
nodes.summary: The impact of a change set on the scoped context is reported from git — the documents, the scopes below them, moves with their ancestry, tracked sources to review, and stale projections — and an unrelated change reports nothing

nodes.label: docs/claims/context-selection-budget.md
nodes.summary: The assembled context obeys a line budget, and every section it drops is named

nodes.label: docs/claims/context-selection-counted.md
nodes.summary: What the context compiler selects is counted, not estimated

nodes.label: docs/claims/continuity-reachable.md
nodes.summary: Every continuity store is proven reachable through its own command

nodes.label: docs/claims/cost-per-outcome.md
nodes.summary: Cost per accepted outcome will be reported from measured data only

nodes.label: docs/claims/dag-validation.md
nodes.summary: A cycle, a self-dependency and a dependency on an issue that does not exist are each refused by name

nodes.label: docs/claims/decision-attribution.md
nodes.summary: A decision record without a task, a head and a reason is reported

nodes.label: docs/claims/decision-record.md
nodes.summary: A decision is recorded with its reason, and superseded rather than edited

nodes.label: docs/claims/deployment-contract-refuses-by-name.md
nodes.summary: A deployment that breaks its closed contract is refused by doctor with the reason named

nodes.label: docs/claims/derivation-one-graph.md
nodes.summary: Every committed derived artifact is regenerated by one command in dependency order and checked by one read-only command

nodes.label: docs/claims/derived-data-current.md
nodes.summary: A commit whose derived data is behind its canonical inputs is refused before it exists

nodes.label: docs/claims/derived-not-declared.md
nodes.summary: What the tool knows about itself is written once and derived everywhere else

nodes.label: docs/claims/dispatcher-wiring.md
nodes.summary: Wiring is found in a hook or in any subhook of the directory it dispatches to

nodes.label: docs/claims/distribution-canonical-model.md
nodes.summary: Every platform, artifact name and installation URL is derived from one model, and a projection that disagrees with it is refused

nodes.label: docs/claims/divergence-label.md
nodes.summary: State read back is labelled exact, advanced, diverged or different_context against git

nodes.label: docs/claims/doctrine-class-decides.md
nodes.summary: A doctrine's class decides whether a violation stops the command

nodes.label: docs/claims/doctrine-registry.md
nodes.summary: Every enforced rule is declared once, and doctor proves it is reached

nodes.label: docs/claims/drift-watch.md
nodes.summary: watch reports policy, projection, state, scope, handover, verification, staleness and retention drift

nodes.label: docs/claims/economics-claims-gated.md
nodes.summary: An unsupported savings claim is refused

nodes.label: docs/claims/effort-escalation.md
nodes.summary: Escalating reasoning effort after repeated blocked attempts is recorded rather than assumed

nodes.label: docs/claims/event-vocabulary.md
nodes.summary: The ledger's event vocabulary is closed, on the way in and on the way out

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-a-crate-binary-that-ran-nothing-is-not-a-pass.md
nodes.summary: A crate test binary that ran no test or only a filtered subset is recorded as a skip, one with a failed test as a failure and one that printed no result as an error, whatever colour codes its output carries, and what no claim can name yet is listed as dropped

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-a-failure-outranks-an-absence.md
nodes.summary: A rule with a failing test reads failing whatever its other tests say

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-a-recording-is-a-typed-run.md
nodes.summary: Every recording yields a run record naming its commit, the tree each report's run measured, its totals and what was absent, dropped or unknown, and a coverage summary joins it only bound to the commit and tree it was measured on

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-a-skip-is-not-run.md
nodes.summary: A test that declined to run reads not run with a detail saying it declined, and a test that errored or timed out reads failing

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-currency-is-not-collapsed.md
nodes.summary: A run recorded against this commit and a run whose inputs merely have not changed since are reported as different states, never as one

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-gates-done.md
nodes.summary: An issue cannot be completed while a required piece of evidence is missing

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-judged-at-the-presented-revision.md
nodes.summary: A claim reads proven only when its run is contained in the presented revision, nothing but the ledger changed since, and both trees were their commits

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-local-recording-stays-local.md
nodes.summary: A recording made with --ledger local writes only the ignored local ledger, changes no tracked file and moves no verdict

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-navigates-both-ways.md
nodes.summary: Every claim names the test meant to settle it and every test names the claims it is meant to settle, from one derivation

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-partial-run-preserves-the-rest.md
nodes.summary: Recording one test's result never erases the evidence recorded for any other test

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-proof-is-an-execution.md
nodes.summary: A claim's proof is an execution that was recorded with the commit it ran against, not a test path that resolves

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-recorded-in-ci.md
nodes.summary: CI records what it ran, with the run it happened in, and the site publishes it with the commit it proves

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-subject-commands-agree-with-the-command-pages.md
nodes.summary: The behavioural and negative tests the subject index names for a command are exactly the ones its command page lists, both read from the first coverage and negative header of each case

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-subjects-are-derived.md
nodes.summary: Every claim, rule, feature, command, capability, MCP tool and use case the repository declares is an evidence subject whose members and tests are derived from declarations that already exist, and a committed subject index that differs from that derivation is refused

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-tree-is-measured-by-the-run.md
nodes.summary: A recorded execution carries the commit and the tree that its run's own measurement stated, a measurement that names the report it belongs to and never hides a tracked change; a measurement of another commit or another report is refused, a local measurement that names no report is refused, a CI report without a measurement is refused, and a report recorded without one carries an unknown tree, which never reads proven

nodes.label: docs/claims/evidence-unsupported-guarantee-is-reported.md
nodes.summary: A claim that declares a guarantee no recorded run supports is named by a gate rather than displayed as guaranteed

nodes.label: docs/claims/executable-reference-derived.md
nodes.summary: The site's pages about the Rust executable are derived from the registry, and a capability that joins or leaves it gains or loses its page from the generators alone

nodes.label: docs/claims/execution-cache-equivalence.md
nodes.summary: A cached capability of the Rust executable answers the same value uncached, cold and warm, a hit runs no handler, errors and commands are never cached, and the key carries the registry fingerprint

nodes.label: docs/claims/execution-waves.md
nodes.summary: Execution waves are computed from the graph, and issues in one wave that touch the same paths are reported as serialised

nodes.label: docs/claims/exit-code-contract.md
nodes.summary: Exit codes are a contract, and no code means "warn and continue"

nodes.label: docs/claims/finish-contract.md
nodes.summary: finish evaluates the finish contract line by line and refuses when any line is unmet

nodes.label: docs/claims/finish-refusal-is-recorded.md
nodes.summary: every refused finish appends a task.refused event naming the outcome claimed, the unmet count and the doctrines that refused, and finish --check writes none

nodes.label: docs/claims/generated-artifacts-typed.md
nodes.summary: Every generated artifact declares the document it projects, the encoding it is written in, the schema its content satisfies and its source, and a structured document is written in every encoding it is committed in from one value

nodes.label: docs/claims/generated-projections-checked.md
nodes.summary: The committed projections, the OpenAPI document, the capability reference and the allow-lists, are regenerated from the registry and the schemas, and generate --check refuses a stale one

nodes.label: docs/claims/git-identity.md
nodes.summary: Identity fields on every state record are computed from git and never authored

nodes.label: docs/claims/github-projection-gated.md
nodes.summary: A projection that stops being applied turns a build red, and a gate that cannot reach GitHub reports that it cannot rather than passing

nodes.label: docs/claims/github-projection.md
nodes.summary: GitHub milestones and issues are generated from the canonical model, and a hand-edited generated region is reported rather than overwritten

nodes.label: docs/claims/handover-record.md
nodes.summary: handover writes an append-only record with computed front matter and required sections

nodes.label: docs/claims/history-ledger-read.md
nodes.summary: The ledger is readable back as operational history

nodes.label: docs/claims/hot-path-no-rebuild.md
nodes.summary: After startup, no MCP or HTTP request of the Rust executable scans the repository, builds the index or the registry, derives a schema or builds a projection, and perf.counters proves it

nodes.label: docs/claims/init-refuses.md
nodes.summary: Installing into a repository that already has an installation is refused

nodes.label: docs/claims/install-command-is-derived.md
nodes.summary: The documented one-line install command is composed from the model's parts, and a document that states a different one fails the suite

nodes.label: docs/claims/installer-verifies-before-installing.md
nodes.summary: The installer verifies an artifact's digest and inspects its archive before anything is unpacked, and any failure leaves the previous installation working

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-closes-github-milestones.md
nodes.summary: A milestone will be closed on GitHub only once the intents it realises are satisfied

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-cockpit-pages.md
nodes.summary: The Cockpit shows every intent with its derived stage at /cockpit/intents, and one intent's criteria, evidence, serving issues and realising work at /cockpit/intents/<id>

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-command-deployment-evidence.md
nodes.summary: A criterion settled by a command or by a deployment will be met by recorded evidence

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-criteria-covered.md
nodes.summary: Once work exists under an intent, a criterion no issue serves, an issue under its milestones that serves nothing and a link to a criterion that does not exist are each refused by name

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-in-session-context.md
nodes.summary: A task that names the issue or the intent it serves is briefed with what that intent asks of the work, and a handover tells the next worker when the intent moved

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-links-resolve.md
nodes.summary: An intent whose criterion names evidence that resolves to nothing is refused by name

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-plan-reviewed.md
nodes.summary: A gap that leaves a criterion unanswered is refused, and an issue serving an intent that started without a critique or while a blocking finding is open fails intent validation

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-preflight-names-the-intent.md
nodes.summary: Asked before work on an issue, `intent preflight` names the intents the issue serves with the governance that applies, or refuses naming the cause

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-realization-held-to-evidence.md
nodes.summary: The work realising an intent is joined across sessions, providers and handovers, and an intent whose milestones are all closed while a criterion's evidence fails is refused naming that criterion

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-refused-at-plan-start.md
nodes.summary: Where the policy requires binding, starting an issue or a task that serves an intent with no critique, or with a blocking finding open, is refused when it is started rather than reported afterwards

nodes.label: docs/claims/intent-stage-derived.md
nodes.summary: An intent's stage is derived from the milestones that realise it and each criterion from the evidence ledger, and it is satisfied only while every criterion has a current passing run

nodes.label: docs/claims/interfaces-are-projections.md
nodes.summary: MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI, the capabilities commands and the generated reference are derived from the registry, and a change to one definition reaches every one of them

nodes.label: docs/claims/knowledge-derivation-is-idempotent.md
nodes.summary: A second derivation over the same evidence writes nothing, says so, and leaves the working tree unchanged

nodes.label: docs/claims/knowledge-derived-at-the-boundary.md
nodes.summary: A provider's end event and its compaction event derive the knowledge the episode produced into candidate records, from the ledger and git and never from a conversation

nodes.label: docs/claims/knowledge-failure-is-recorded.md
nodes.summary: A policy switch that is off derives nothing and says so; a derivation that fails inside a provider hook is recorded as a failed event and the hook still exits 0

nodes.label: docs/claims/knowledge-integrity.md
nodes.summary: Every knowledge record is schema-valid, uniquely identified, evidenced when verified, resolves every reference it names, and carries no conversation

nodes.label: docs/claims/knowledge-promotion-is-an-act.md
nodes.summary: verified is written only by promote with evidence on stdin or by a person editing the file, never by the deriver

nodes.label: docs/claims/knowledge-served-on-every-surface.md
nodes.summary: The candidates awaiting review, one record by id with its references resolved, and the derivation status of the checkout answer with the same content over the command line, HTTP and MCP

nodes.label: docs/claims/knowledge-writer-observed.md
nodes.summary: A repository in which episodes close and no knowledge derivation follows within the stale threshold is reported as a stopped writer

nodes.label: docs/claims/landing-page-is-a-projection.md
nodes.summary: The homepage names nothing of its own

nodes.label: docs/claims/ledger-integrity.md
nodes.summary: Every line of the ledger is a well-formed event

nodes.label: docs/claims/legacy-migration.md
nodes.summary: A repository on the pre-.ai layout is migrated once, explicitly, with a previewed plan and a verified backup of its local state, and the command is idempotent afterwards

nodes.label: docs/claims/live-scenario-evidence-is-local.md
nodes.summary: A live scenario is not selected by a bare usecase run, its evidence is written under the ignored local half, and it never raises a command to covered

nodes.label: docs/claims/live-scenario-is-read-only.md
nodes.summary: A live scenario may only run commands share/commands.yaml declares read-only, names no setup, and asserts an obligation only where something owes one

nodes.label: docs/claims/local-state-ignored.md
nodes.summary: Checkout-local state lives under .ai/local/, is ignored by git, and is absent on a fresh clone or worktree

nodes.label: docs/claims/mcp-client-always-served.md
nodes.summary: A client that starts the MCP server from a checkout whose executable is missing or stale is served by the installed release when it is of this tree's generation and told so, and is otherwise refused with exit 12 naming the explicit build; nothing is built

nodes.label: docs/claims/mcp-client-autostart.md
nodes.summary: An MCP client opened in the repository starts the server itself, through the client configurations at the root and bin/majordomus-mcp, without ever building the executable

nodes.label: docs/claims/mcp-data-driven.md
nodes.summary: What the MCP server serves is decided by the manifest, the declared source classes and each file's front matter, so an object added to the layer is served with no change to the executable

nodes.label: docs/claims/mcp-degraded-not-silent.md
nodes.summary: A file of the layer the MCP server cannot read is excluded with a diagnostic naming its path and the index says it is degraded, never silently smaller

nodes.label: docs/claims/mcp-lease-lost.md
nodes.summary: A server whose lease was taken over says so on the endpoint every reader probes, refuses to take on a new client, and reports that what its health describes is another process; the sessions it already had continue and it ends with them

nodes.label: docs/claims/mcp-lease-resilience.md
nodes.summary: Nothing a client leaves behind locks another client out of the shared server; a corrupt, empty, stale or abandoned lease is taken over and named, a client that cannot share is served alone with the reason logged, and a signal removes the lease before the server dies

nodes.label: docs/claims/mcp-peers.md
nodes.summary: Every client attached to the shared server is a peer named by its own initialize, listed by majordomus_peers, and majordomus_announce tells the others what it is working on and which paths it expects to touch

nodes.label: docs/claims/mcp-shared-server.md
nodes.summary: One shared server serves a repository: the first majordomus mcp binds loopback HTTP with Swagger UI and MCP over HTTP beside its stdio session and logs the URL, every later one attaches to it, and it ends when the last client leaves

nodes.label: docs/claims/mcp-stdio-surface.md
nodes.summary: The Rust executable serves the repository's AI layer to an MCP client over stdio, with protocol frames alone on stdout

nodes.label: docs/claims/mcp-uri-resolution.md
nodes.summary: A majordomus:// URI resolves the same way through the MCP resource read, the majordomus_get tool and the HTTP object route, and majordomus://repository answers repository.info as a JSON document tagged builtin

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-claims-cross-runtime.md
nodes.summary: An exclusive claim made on one runtime excludes an overlapping claim on every linked runtime, and concurrent claims resolve to one named winner everywhere

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-compaction-keeps-what-is-live.md
nodes.summary: Compacting the cooperation journal changes nothing live — a handover nobody has taken keeps its stream for a bounded retention, who took a handover and who answered a review stay with them, and a compacted runtime that beats again is fetched again whole

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-cooperation-links.md
nodes.summary: Two runtimes of one repository link only through a signed, replay-protected handshake that checks protocol, repository identity and trust, and every refusal is typed and visible

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-declared-is-held.md
nodes.summary: An enabled mesh declaration whose shared server did not activate the mesh is a failed `runtime` check of `mesh doctor` (exit 10) carrying the server's reason, and a `Mesh: DECLARED ENABLED BUT NOT ACTIVE` line in the session-start briefing — never a quiet off; and this repository's committed declaration is tracked, enabled, allowlists the fleet and names a hub

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-firewall-is-derived.md
nodes.summary: The inbound admissions a mesh declaration implies on a machine — the multicast group's port, the declared hub ports whose address is the machine's, the server's port beyond loopback — are derived from the declaration by `majordomus mesh firewall`, which names the host's firewall backend, the commands that admit them and the firewall's own verdict, exits 10 when a rule is observed missing or the kernel logged a drop toward those ports, and whose `apply` runs the commands only as root and never over HTTP or MCP; `mesh doctor` carries the same verdict as its `firewall` check

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-liveness-expiry.md
nodes.summary: A runtime that stops beating — crashed, killed or partitioned — expires on its peers within the declared expiry, its claims stop excluding, and its restart reconnects as the same runtime without a duplicate

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-network-acceptance.md
nodes.summary: Separate Linux nodes on a real network discover each other by multicast, link, share claims and handovers, and recover from a partition and a crash, in a lab CI runs

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-observation-not-authority.md
nodes.summary: A discovered node gains no execution and no authorization from being heard; only signed traffic from a linked node may change mesh state, and trust labels records under an explicit policy that defaults to deny_unknown

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-off-by-default.md
nodes.summary: No mesh discovery socket opens until the repository commits an enabled mesh declaration, and a disabled or absent declaration is reported as the reason, not an error

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-one-registry.md
nodes.summary: Every discovery observation converges into one bounded registry, deduplicated by node and runtime identity across sources, replay-protected per instance, and every surface projects that registry and holds no peers of its own

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-repository-isolation.md
nodes.summary: Runtimes serving different repositories never form a cooperative link, even when they discover each other

nodes.label: docs/claims/mesh-three-runtime-convergence.md
nodes.summary: Runtimes linked only through a relay converge on one state digest, each event held once, with no replication loop

nodes.label: docs/claims/minimum-context.md
nodes.summary: A profile declares which context a worker should load and no more

nodes.label: docs/claims/models-no-secret-fields.md
nodes.summary: The model catalogue reports whether a vendor's named credential variable is set and can carry no secret value — the schema has no field one could hide in

nodes.label: docs/claims/models-one-declaration.md
nodes.summary: Vendors and models are declared once in share/models.yaml, and the CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and Cockpit render that one declaration with no model name of their own

nodes.label: docs/claims/models-routing-explains-itself.md
nodes.summary: A routing decision names why the selected model was selected and, for every excluded model, the first check it failed — the same answer for the same question, with no hidden state

nodes.label: docs/claims/new-code-is-covered.md

nodes.label: docs/claims/no-counts-in-context.md
nodes.summary: A hardcoded count in the always-loaded file is a failure

nodes.label: docs/claims/no-network.md
nodes.summary: The shell tool performs no network call, evaluates no generated text and deletes nothing recursively; its one declared request is the loopback peer probe

nodes.label: docs/claims/no-silent-overwrite.md
nodes.summary: A hand-edited instruction file is never silently overwritten

nodes.label: docs/claims/no-transcripts.md
nodes.summary: A handover is a state record, not a transcript

nodes.label: docs/claims/obligation-closure.md

nodes.label: docs/claims/obligation-establishment.md
nodes.summary: An obligation whose fact the tool can hold is established live rather than recorded, and a hand-recorded line neither discharges it nor rescues it

nodes.label: docs/claims/observatory-draws-nothing-it-did-not-read.md
nodes.summary: The Observatory draws nothing it did not read

nodes.label: docs/claims/open-question-gate.md
nodes.summary: An unresolved question blocks acceptance, and an unparseable entry is a failure

nodes.label: docs/claims/openapi-inferred.md

nodes.label: docs/claims/overlap-report.md
nodes.summary: Overlap between parallel workers is computed on claimed paths in both containment directions

nodes.label: docs/claims/personal-layer-changes-nothing-shared.md

nodes.label: docs/claims/pointer-integrity.md
nodes.summary: Every repository-relative reference in the always-loaded file is proven to resolve

nodes.label: docs/claims/policy-parse.md
nodes.summary: The canonical policy is parsed and rejected if it contains an unknown key

nodes.label: docs/claims/product-domains-derived.md
nodes.summary: The product is filed under domains, and the domain lists nothing

nodes.label: docs/claims/product-features-discovered.md
nodes.summary: A product feature is discovered, never registered

nodes.label: docs/claims/product-projection-public-safe.md
nodes.summary: The public dataset carries only fields somebody allowed

nodes.label: docs/claims/product-references-resolve.md
nodes.summary: A reference that resolves to nothing is an error, not a broken link

nodes.label: docs/claims/product-surfaces-derived.md
nodes.summary: What a feature is on is derived; what it is for is written

nodes.label: docs/claims/profile-axes.md
nodes.summary: Capability class, reasoning effort, output verbosity, context and verification are five independent axes

nodes.label: docs/claims/profile-validate.md
nodes.summary: Every profile is parsed, its unknown keys rejected, and the default profile proven to exist

nodes.label: docs/claims/project-schema.md
nodes.summary: Milestones and issues are canonical repository files, and a key nobody reads is an error

nodes.label: docs/claims/project-status-derived.md
nodes.summary: Issue and milestone status is derived from recorded facts and is stored nowhere

nodes.label: docs/claims/projected-record-edit-is-landable.md
nodes.summary: A pull request that edits a projected plan record is not refused because GitHub does not show the edit yet, and the trunk is refused for it once a declared window has passed

nodes.label: docs/claims/projection-fingerprint.md
nodes.summary: Every generated instruction file carries its own stamp, and a hand edit is detected

nodes.label: docs/claims/projection-generation.md
nodes.summary: Provider instruction files are generated from the one policy, deterministically

nodes.label: docs/claims/prompt-asset.md
nodes.summary: A prompt renders against a closed set of tokens, and an unknown token is an error

nodes.label: docs/claims/prompt-assets.md
nodes.summary: Every prompt asset renders, and an unknown token is a failure

nodes.label: docs/claims/prompt-capture.md
nodes.summary: A provider hook captures the person's raw prompts below the model, as a record and a rendering, and doctor proves it by running it

nodes.label: docs/claims/prompt-continuity.md
nodes.summary: A captured prompt names the episode it belongs to or records that none could be resolved; the archive is private, bounded and free of credential material

nodes.label: docs/claims/provider-capability-evidence.md
nodes.summary: What each provider can do about the session lifecycle and prompt capture is one declaration with a citation per cell, every surface projects it, and no provider the declaration names goes unreported

nodes.label: docs/claims/provider-projections-one-renderer.md
nodes.summary: The provider bootstraps are a target of `majordomus generate`, rendered by one renderer, and `generate --check` refuses a stale one in CI

nodes.label: docs/claims/published-translation-is-declared.md
nodes.summary: A published page in another language is declared, and declares itself

nodes.label: docs/claims/reasoning-survives-the-session.md
nodes.summary: A decision and its provenance survive the session: the next session finds them in its context and handover, reuses a standing conclusion instead of consulting again, and reopens it only on new evidence

nodes.label: docs/claims/reasoning-works-with-no-advisor.md
nodes.summary: Majordomus reasons, decides, implements and validates with no advisor at all: absent advisors are reported as ordinary state, material uncertainty gets a structured local review, and the conclusion claims no independent review

nodes.label: docs/claims/record-resolution.md
nodes.summary: The right prior record is resolved by worktree and branch, and an unrelated one is never offered

nodes.label: docs/claims/record-retention.md
nodes.summary: Rotating the ledger archives the oldest lines and never deletes them

nodes.label: docs/claims/record-search.md
nodes.summary: Durable records are searchable literally, across kinds, without an index

nodes.label: docs/claims/region-projection.md
nodes.summary: A projection can own only the region between its markers

nodes.label: docs/claims/release-archive-shape.md
nodes.summary: A release archive carries every path once and carries nothing but files and directories

nodes.label: docs/claims/release-is-complete-or-absent.md
nodes.summary: A release publishes an artifact for every supported target or it is not published

nodes.label: docs/claims/release-prerelease-channel.md
nodes.summary: A tag with a pre-release part is published as a prerelease, recorded on the prerelease channel, and never resolved as the stable release, so an unpinned installer and a node that follows stable keep the highest stable version

nodes.label: docs/claims/reproduce-command.md
nodes.summary: Every finding carries the command that reproduces it

nodes.label: docs/claims/retention-caps.md
nodes.summary: The append-only ledger and handover store have retention caps that are checked

nodes.label: docs/claims/review-is-never-fabricated.md
nodes.summary: A session cannot claim review it did not get: a consultation must name an advisor its recorded plan selected, a conclusion's review is computed, and reasoning check and doctor refuse a forged record, provider coupling, a model credential in CI and a refused claim in a document

nodes.label: docs/claims/roadmap-derived.md
nodes.summary: The roadmap is derived from milestone state, and no document may be a second authority for it

nodes.label: docs/claims/routing.md
nodes.summary: Routing recommendations will be derived from measured cost and outcome data

nodes.label: docs/claims/rule-exemption-carries-its-reason.md
nodes.summary: A rule that no program can express says so, with the reason, and is counted apart

nodes.label: docs/claims/rule-proof-is-named-and-resolves.md
nodes.summary: Every rule names what proves it, and every path it names is in the tree

nodes.label: docs/claims/rule-resolution.md
nodes.summary: The effective rule set is resolved as a dependency graph in a deterministic order, and a set that does not resolve is applied by nothing

nodes.label: docs/claims/rule-state-is-derived-from-what-ran.md
nodes.summary: A rule's proof state is derived from the tree and the ledger together

nodes.label: docs/claims/runtime-adapters.md
nodes.summary: Opt-in runtime adapters will clamp read size, output size and fan-out from profile-derived limits

nodes.label: docs/claims/rust-binary-artifact.md
nodes.summary: The Rust executable the rust gate built is published as an artifact with its provenance, and every Rust case drives the executable MAJORDOMUS_BIN names instead of building one

nodes.label: docs/claims/rust-coverage-floor.md
nodes.summary: Coverage of the Rust crate is measured with test code out of the denominator, on every change that can affect the crate and on every push to master, and the build fails under the floor in scripts/rust-coverage-threshold or under the session/continuity domain's own floor in scripts/session-coverage-threshold

nodes.label: docs/claims/rust-evidence-gates.md
nodes.summary: Every gate the Rust executable must pass is one script, scripts/rust-check, and CI runs that script on every change that can reach the crate

nodes.label: docs/claims/rust-hot-path-benchmarks.md
nodes.summary: The paths of the Rust executable that scale with the repository carry criterion benchmarks that build on every push, and every executable capability declares its benchmark policy, required or waived for a typed reason

nodes.label: docs/claims/rustdoc-complete.md
nodes.summary: Every exported item has its rustdoc page at its derived route, and no page is an orphan

nodes.label: docs/claims/rustdoc-composed-from-the-topology.md
nodes.summary: The site build composes every published static surface from the committed topology, and refuses one whose artifact is absent

nodes.label: docs/claims/rustdoc-discoverable.md
nodes.summary: The crate's rustdoc is a web surface at /rustdoc, declared from the crate and served from the tree its producer wrote

nodes.label: docs/claims/rustdoc-published.md
nodes.summary: The crate's rustdoc is published at /rustdoc with the site, built from the commit the site names

nodes.label: docs/claims/rustdoc-referenced.md
nodes.summary: Every builtin module's page links its page in the crate's reference

nodes.label: docs/claims/rustdoc-verified-live.md
nodes.summary: A rustdoc tree built from another commit is refused, before publication and at the public URL

nodes.label: docs/claims/schema-driven-kinds.md
nodes.summary: How each declarative kind is read and which keys it may carry is data read at run time, and a repository adds a kind with its JSON Schema without a code change

nodes.label: docs/claims/scope-declared.md
nodes.summary: What a worker reads of the repository is declared once in .ai/repo/scope.yaml, out wins over in, and the Rust executable discovers, indexes and serves nothing outside it

nodes.label: docs/claims/scope-enforcement.md
nodes.summary: A touched file outside the claimed scope is a failure, not a warning

nodes.label: docs/claims/scoped-task.md
nodes.summary: A task is started with a declared file scope and a profile, and only one task is active per checkout

nodes.label: docs/claims/semantic-retrieval.md
nodes.summary: Ranked or semantic retrieval over durable records is deliberately not implemented

nodes.label: docs/claims/session-lifecycle.md
nodes.summary: A provider hook opens and closes the execution episode, and the context it was given at the open is frozen beside it

nodes.label: docs/claims/session-observability.md
nodes.summary: The session subsystem can be watched, not only used: every open episode, what cannot close itself, and which commit the process is answering about

nodes.label: docs/claims/session-records.md
nodes.summary: A closed execution episode is a shared object of the layer, written by the tool from git and the ledger, valid against a contract that admits no conversation and no absolute path, and discovered rather than registered

nodes.label: docs/claims/session-start-prompt.md
nodes.summary: A bare claude in a supervised repository starts with the repository's session-start prompt as its first message, and a run with an argument, outside such a repository, with the opt-out, or with a prompt that cannot be rendered is left exactly as it was

nodes.label: docs/claims/shared-policy.md
nodes.summary: One policy will be shared across repositories and workers

nodes.label: docs/claims/site-deploy-one-path.md
nodes.summary: The site is deployed by one script, from a terminal or from the Pages workflow, and the deploy names its source

nodes.label: docs/claims/site-deploys-from-verified-run.md
nodes.summary: Publication is gated on everything that can make the published site wrong and waits for nothing else; the checks that decide whether a change may merge run beside it on the same commit, not in front of it

nodes.label: docs/claims/site-registry-dataset.md
nodes.summary: The site's Registry page is rendered from a dataset `majordomus generate site` derives from the registry, and `generate --check` refuses a stale one

nodes.label: docs/claims/skill-catalogue.md
nodes.summary: A skill is one directory under the skills section, discovered by the source class both readers share, so that adding the file is the whole registration

nodes.label: docs/claims/skill-check.md
nodes.summary: Every skill is validated against the allow-list generated from its schema, its directory, its sections and its references, and a repository with no skills is reported rather than passed

nodes.label: docs/claims/skill-site-projection.md
nodes.summary: The website's skills section is rendered from the skills catalogue, one page per skill carrying its own body and examples, and a removed or renamed skill leaves nothing behind

nodes.label: docs/claims/suite-parallel.md
nodes.summary: The behavioural suite runs a bounded number of cases at a time with the serial runner's semantics, a case that writes into the checkout declares itself exclusive and runs alone, and the parallel phase fails naming the paths when the checkout changed under it

nodes.label: docs/claims/task-commit-attribution.md
nodes.summary: A task will know which commits it produced, rather than inferring them from a range

nodes.label: docs/claims/task-dependencies.md
nodes.summary: A task record has no dependencies; sequencing between sessions is not represented

nodes.label: docs/claims/telemetry.md
nodes.summary: Execution telemetry will be recorded once a provider exposes it honestly

nodes.label: docs/claims/the-closing-question-is-measured.md
nodes.summary: Whether a task added debt, left a branch or a worktree behind, or grew the backlog is answered by the done invariant from git, the debt baselines and the recorded forge observation, measured from where the task started; a reading that was not taken is unknown, never a pass

nodes.label: docs/claims/token-savings-measured.md
nodes.summary: A total-token change is stated only from verified, matched runs

nodes.label: docs/claims/tool-location-independent.md
nodes.summary: The tool runs read-only from any location, and two locations of one version agree about one repository

nodes.label: docs/claims/typed-outcome.md
nodes.summary: An outcome is a value from a closed vocabulary, not free text

nodes.label: docs/claims/ui-dashboard-cites-its-sources.md
nodes.summary: The UI's dashboard names the capability behind every value it shows, and never waits for the queue

nodes.label: docs/claims/use-case-coverage.md
nodes.summary: Every public command is named and run by an active use case, a guaranteed claim or an MCP tool without one is a named gap, and the policy says which gaps fail doctor, check and finish

nodes.label: docs/claims/use-case-evidence.md
nodes.summary: A use case's scenario executes against the real tool in a disposable repository, every step's exit code and output are asserted, and the normalised evidence is what the site shows

nodes.label: docs/claims/use-case-impact.md
nodes.summary: From the files a change touched, the tool names the commands, rules, use cases, scenarios and behavioural cases affected, and scaffolds a draft for a capability no use case covers

nodes.label: docs/claims/vendored-rule-package.md
nodes.summary: The rule baseline is vendored into the repository with a manifest naming every file and its hash, and a hand edit is detected and refused

nodes.label: docs/claims/web-namespaces-reserved.md
nodes.summary: /docs serves this repository's documentation and /swagger serves the Swagger UI, and neither may take the other's mount

nodes.label: docs/claims/web-surface-declared-once.md
nodes.summary: Every web surface is declared once at its producer and resolved into one topology, from which the router, the landing page and the machine-readable index are each projected

nodes.label: docs/claims/why-catalogue-discovered.md
nodes.summary: An operational moment is discovered, never registered

nodes.label: docs/claims/why-diagnosis-explainable.md
nodes.summary: A diagnosis is counting, and it says what it counted

nodes.label: docs/claims/why-references-resolve.md
nodes.summary: Every reference a moment makes resolves

nodes.label: docs/claims/wiring-reconciliation.md
nodes.summary: Every enforcement the policy declares is reconciled against what actually runs

nodes.label: docs/claims/worktree-migration-lossless.md
nodes.summary: A misplaced worktree migrates with its work intact, and proves it

nodes.label: docs/claims/worktree-ownership.md
nodes.summary: A task record names its checkout, and another checkout is never held to its scope

nodes.label: docs/claims/worktree-topology-derived.md
nodes.summary: A branch's worktree path is derived, never registered

nodes.label: completion
nodes.summary: Completion

facts.headline: Done is a contract the repository evaluates line by line. Work is not accepted while any line fails, and a refusal stays on the record.
facts.problem: Done is cheap. A worker can report success before the repository's own checks hold.

nodes.label: context
nodes.summary: Context

facts.headline: Every worker starts from what the repository already knows: the context that applies to its path, the handover the last session left, and the decisions already made.
facts.problem: Agents forget. What one session learned dies with its conversation, and the next one starts over.

nodes.label: coordination
nodes.summary: Coordination

facts.headline: Every worker declares the paths it will touch, sees who else is working and where, and hears about a collision before it is committed.
facts.problem: Agents collide. Parallel workers edit the same paths, or build the same thing twice, without knowing about each other.

nodes.label: evidence
nodes.summary: Evidence

facts.headline: A claim names the test that settles it, a recorded run is judged against the commit it ran at, and a claim with no recorded run says so.
facts.problem: Claims outrun proof. The documentation says one thing, the runtime does another, and nobody can show which is true.

nodes.label: governance
nodes.summary: Governance

facts.headline: The rules are written once, in the repository, projected into every tool's instructions, and a blocking rule stops the command instead of advising it.
facts.problem: Rules drift. Each tool keeps its own instruction file, and a rule nobody wired into enforcement is only a suggestion.

nodes.label: surfaces
nodes.summary: Surfaces

facts.headline: One declaration in the repository becomes the command line, the HTTP API, MCP, the UI, the Cockpit, the documentation and this site, and a projection that disagrees with it fails the build.
facts.problem: Interfaces disagree. The command line, the API, the docs and the website each keep a copy, and the copies drift.

nodes.label: benchmarks
nodes.summary: Every claim about speed is a recorded measurement

facts.headline: Every externally callable operation is timed directly, over MCP and over HTTP, the denominator is generated from the registry, and a regression against the accepted baseline fails the check.

nodes.label: ci
nodes.summary: CI planned from one model, the site deployed from its verified run

facts.headline: A change runs the gates its paths can affect, every gate is the same script a person runs, and the public site is published only from a commit whose derived data proved current.

nodes.label: cockpit
nodes.summary: The Cockpit: the registry rendered for a person

nodes.label: commit
nodes.summary: A commit message is a value this repository judges, not a convention it hopes for

nodes.label: context
nodes.summary: Every directory of the layer carries its contract, and a worker reads what applies

nodes.label: continuity
nodes.summary: Sessions, prompts and handovers that outlive the conversation

facts.headline: A session ends and the work does not: what the next worker needs is a typed record checked against git, not a transcript somebody hopes to find.

nodes.label: coordination
nodes.summary: Several agents on one repository, without stepping on each other

facts.headline: Every worker declares the paths it may touch, every session can see who else is attached and what they announced, and a collision is reported before it is committed.

nodes.label: coverage
nodes.summary: New code is covered, measured once and asked two questions

facts.headline: One coverage measurement, test code out of the denominator, holds a crate floor, a floor over the session/continuity domain, and — the invariant of #214 — every executable line a change touches.

nodes.label: declare-once
nodes.summary: Declare once, derive every interface

facts.headline: A capability is written in one place, and the command line, the HTTP API, the OpenAPI document, MCP, the Cockpit, the reference and this website are projections of it.

nodes.label: deployments
nodes.summary: A deployment is one canonical object, and every artifact built from it is generated from it

facts.headline: The port, the routes and the build inputs of the executable's container image are stated once, and the image definition and its ignore file are projections that cannot drift from it.

nodes.label: doctrine
nodes.summary: Rules a machine decides, wired, tested and CI-blocking

facts.headline: A rule is enforced when a validator decides it, a command runs it, a test proves it and CI blocks on it; anything less is documentation, and the tool knows the difference.

nodes.label: economics
nodes.summary: Token economics, measured from matched runs and never typed

nodes.label: evidence
nodes.summary: A claim is proven by a run that happened, not by a file that exists

nodes.label: finish-contract
nodes.summary: Done is a contract, evaluated line by line and refused when unmet

nodes.label: install
nodes.summary: One command to install, one to initialise, nothing else to trust

facts.headline: The installer downloads one archive for your machine, verifies its digest against the release metadata before unpacking anything, and installs atomically; no git, no Rust, no Node, no root.

nodes.label: interfaces
nodes.summary: One registry over the command line, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI and MCP

facts.headline: Every agent, script and person reads the same repository through the interface it already speaks, and none of the interfaces is maintained by hand.

nodes.label: knowledge
nodes.summary: Decisions and knowledge that compound instead of evaporating

facts.headline: What was decided, why, and what was rejected is recorded where the next session reads it, and a durable decision becomes an architecture record with typed links to what it put in force.

nodes.label: mesh
nodes.summary: Sessions on several machines work one repository without colliding

nodes.label: models
nodes.summary: The models the world offers, declared once and routed with reasons

facts.headline: One declared catalogue of vendors and models — capabilities, context, lifecycle, no fabricated facts — and a routing answer that names why every candidate was chosen or excluded.

nodes.label: observatory
nodes.summary: The Observatory: the repository and its mesh, drawn for a wall

facts.headline: One screen of the UI rotates eight scenes on a display nobody is sitting at, and every mark on it is a value a capability answered; a scene with nothing true to draw says why and is never drawn empty.

nodes.label: planning
nodes.summary: Milestones and issues as data; status derived, never stored

facts.headline: An issue records what happened to it and the engine derives whether it is blocked, ready, active, verifying or done from the dependency graph, so the roadmap cannot disagree with the plan.

nodes.label: policy
nodes.summary: One policy, projected into every tool's instruction file

nodes.label: provenance
nodes.summary: Every record names the commit, the branch and the episode that made it

facts.headline: Who did what, under which task, at which commit, in which session is a ledger the tool writes and a person can read back, not a memory of a conversation.

nodes.label: reasoning
nodes.summary: Reasoning that works with or without advisors, and review that is recorded rather than claimed

facts.headline: Material uncertainty becomes an evidence-backed decision — reviewed by whichever optional advisors are available, decided locally when none are, and carried to the next session as a record.

nodes.label: skills
nodes.summary: Skills are procedures as data, discovered and checked, never registered

facts.headline: A skill is one directory under the layer; adding it is the whole act, and the command line, the website and MCP all read it from the same file.

nodes.label: ui
nodes.summary: majordomus ui: the delivery, for a person

nodes.label: use-cases
nodes.summary: Every use case is executed against the tool, not described

facts.headline: What a person does with the tool is one file with a scenario the tool runs against itself; the page shows that execution, and a public command no use case runs is a gap the tool reports.

nodes.label: why
nodes.summary: The failure modes it answers are objects, not marketing pages

nodes.label: worktrees
nodes.summary: One branch, one worktree, at a path derived from git

facts.headline: A branch's worktree is where git says it is, never where somebody chose to put it, and a misplaced one is a diagnostic with a remedy rather than a mystery.

nodes.label: the-owner-directs-work-from-the-ui
nodes.summary: the-owner-directs-work-from-the-ui

nodes.label: a-brief-is-reconciled-into-the-plan
nodes.summary: An external brief enters as a revision with provenance, and its requirements are reconciled into the one plan

invariants: No second intent, milestone or issue model: reconciliation derives into intent.rs/plan.rs records (ADR 0124)
Nothing in a brief is governance or authorisation; it is untrusted source material
Ingesting never executes; capture proposes, execution stays behind the task lifecycle
A received brief is a campaign (proposed ADR 0180, rule project.no-new-nouns): no kind, command, schema or capability is named intake or pack
Only the evidence machinery says a criterion is satisfied; reconciliation reads the verdict and never writes or judges one
non_goals: Autonomous merge, release or deploy pre-authorised by a pasted document
Reading conversations without a person's act (rule of a-session-leaves-what-it-observed)
Keeping a conversation's bytes under .ai/repo/ or campaigns/ (rule project.never-store-transcripts)
A second store beside campaigns/, or a second duplicate detector beside I3254

nodes.label: a-browser-computes-what-the-server-verifies
nodes.summary: A browser computes for a project with the same code the server runs, and nothing it returns is trusted until the server has recomputed it

invariants: One implementation per computation, in the portable core; the browser runs it as wasm32 and the executable links it, and an executed fixture decides whether they agree
A browser's result is a claim; only the server's recomputation verifies it, and agreement among browsers is never proof
A browser holds no mesh key, takes no claim, appends nothing to the journal and writes nothing until an authentication the owner accepts exists (ADR 0126, ADR 0170)
Participation is opt-in, revocable and visible; nothing computes in a page a person did not ask to compute
non_goals: A second mesh, a browser-specific scheduler or a second capability registry
Arbitrary code from a peer; only the core's own functions run

nodes.label: a-build-reuses-what-the-mesh-already-built
nodes.summary: A build reuses what any node of its platform already built or fetched, and is exactly as correct when nothing can be reused

invariants: A miss, a down store, a slow store, a refused credential or a corrupt entry costs time, never correctness (rule project.cache-is-invisible); the build then runs exactly as it did without the cache
A cold, a warm and a bypassed run leave the same result, and MAJORDOMUS_BUILD_CACHE=off bypasses every level (rule project.cache-is-invisible)
The key is derived from what the repository and the machine already say (lockfiles, toolchain executables, host triple, the environment that changes the output); nothing in a key is typed by hand
A store is used only when a trusted node offers it in a signed, expiring record (ADR 0157 decision 2); presence on a port is never trust
An archive is restored only after its content digest matches the one recorded when it was saved, and only inside its target directory
No credential, private address or secret appears in git, .ai, an answer, a log line, a process environment, a page or a document (ADR 0157 decision 7)
Every store and every local level is bounded by declared policy and measured by a command (rule project.accumulation-is-measured); a restore passes the same free-space floor as a build
non_goals: Distributed compilation (sccache-dist, icecream)
Mandatory mesh discovery on the derive critical path
A hit across platforms: a triple shares only with itself, except where the cached thing is platform-independent source
Writing a user's ~/.cargo/config.toml or shell profile
Reaching the store from GitHub's runners, which already cache through actions/cache

nodes.label: a-change-is-judged-in-minutes
nodes.summary: A change is derived in under a second and judged in minutes, and nothing that could have changed is skipped

invariants: The full derive (scripts/derive --full, introduced by I2525) and scripts/derive-check stay the oracle; an incremental result is byte-identical to a full one
A reused result is reported as inputs_unchanged, never as proven (ADR 0041)
Unknown impact selects everything; a cache miss or corruption costs time, never correctness (rule project.cache-is-invisible)
The executable's generation identity is checked on every reuse (rule project.a-tool-that-cannot-match-the-tree-refuses)
Invalidation follows git index semantics; mtime is a hint only (rule project.a-derive-sees-what-the-commit-will)
non_goals: A cold full rebuild under one second
A second derivation engine, scheduler or cache registry beside generate.rs and scripts/ci-plan (rules project.no-new-nouns, project.derived-once)
Moving a required check to nightly or making it advisory to reach a number
Mandatory mesh discovery on the derive critical path

nodes.label: a-change-reconciles-what-it-affects
nodes.summary: A prompt, a change or an inference is reconciled with the intents, issues, knowledge and evidence it affects, deterministically, under one identity on every surface

non_goals: A service, framework or crate named after the Cognitive Fabric, or renaming the product
Automatic promotion, rejection or relation of knowledge; promotion stays a person's act (ADR 0091)
Cheap local model classification before the local-inference work on feature/a-local-runtime-is-observed lands
A filesystem watcher or a daemon beside the shared server
A stored prompt-to-intent match record; the match and the slice are derived on read
Authentication of remote callers
Mesh work assignment (I3198, I3199) and provider-session usage accounting (milestone every-sessions-usage-is-observed)
The discovery, enforcement and delivery waves of the pack (prompts/01, prompts/06_ENFORCEMENT.md, prompts/07_DELIVERY.md), whose reuse matrices were not part of this plan's input

nodes.label: a-claim-stands-only-on-its-evidence
nodes.summary: A claim that something is enforced, tested or delivered stands only on recorded evidence that would have caught it being false

invariants: A blocking rule is reported proven only by a recorded run of a case in which its violation is refused
Proof states are computed from the executions recorded for the presented revision (the CI run's own record, or the tracked ledger where that revision's run is tracked); no surface types a verdict
Unknown, not run and stale are never rendered as pass
A merge past the required check, a protection that no longer requires the verdict, and a rule resting on a proposed ADR are each reported
non_goals: A second rule engine, evidence store or \"rules self-check\" command beside rules/mod.rs, lib/doctrine.sh and scripts/ci/rule-proof-check
A global 100 percent coverage threshold; the differential gate stays the changed-code invariant
Blocking every change on mutation testing

nodes.label: a-person-runs-majordomus-from-a-phone
nodes.summary: A person runs Majordomus from a phone with nothing missing that the desktop offers

invariants: One component, one route set and one design declaration serve every width; a narrow width is a projection, never a second UI
The widths a surface is held at are the ones the design declares, never a list kept by a test
non_goals: A native or separate mobile application
Hiding a function below a width

nodes.label: a-provider-carries-the-contract-natively
nodes.summary: Each agent client enforces and observes the repository's contract through its own extension points, generated from the registry

invariants: Every client artefact is a generated projection stamped with its source; a hand edit fails the drift gate
A client's own memory or settings never become canonical state
Personal settings, permission modes and model choice are never projected (ADR 0140, ADR 0145)
No client binary is patched
non_goals: An agent runtime, marketplace or scheduler of Majordomus's own
A Gemini adapter, deferred until the Codex adapter (I3303) settles the adapter shape; the verified Gemini evidence and the SessionEnd and PreCompress caveats in share/providers.yaml stay
Loading code from outside the repository: external scripted capabilities belong to repository-automation-is-typed

nodes.label: a-session-leaves-what-it-observed
nodes.summary: Every managed session leaves what it observed, and the repository groups and routes it without being asked

non_goals: Creating issues, rules, ADRs or pull requests from a candidate; acting on a route is a later milestone and an act
Deriving friction from task.refused or task.gate; which of those lines are friction rather than the tool working needs its own measurement
Sending a candidate to another repository; nothing leaves the checkout
Classifying by an LLM; an agent may record observations and act on routes, and the core needs none
Codex and Gemini lifecycle hooks; an observation needs an open episode, which any provider opens with session start or an MCP attach
Where candidates are written on a trunk that accepts only pull requests (I1984); grouping on read holds wherever they are

nodes.label: a-session-proceeds-through-the-mesh
nodes.summary: Every supervised session realises intents by proceeding through the mesh, unasked, resumably and watched

invariants: No new store, scheduler, journal kind or registry: state is the intent, the plan, the ledger and the mesh journal
Every provider projection is generated from one canonical declaration; a hand-edited copy fails generate --check
A session never stops or kills what it does not own (ADR 0200)
Every wait has a deadline and a recovery path
non_goals: Push assignment of work to peers before I3198
Changing a profile automatically from inferred routing
Editing a person's .claude/settings.json or personal commands

nodes.label: a-session-record-says-what-it-served
nodes.summary: A session's lifecycle has one writer, and its record says what it served and whether it is complete

invariants: One implementation of each lifecycle transition; shell parses arguments and renders output only (ADR 0047, ADR 0052)
No transcript, prompt text or conversation reaches a record (rule project.never-store-transcripts)
Episode state never reads task state (ADR 0052)
No second session store (ADR 0014, ADR 0047)
non_goals: An LLM-written summary as an authority
A session/v2 island other hooks could bypass
Reopening the exactly-once close, the composed body or freshness, which are in force

nodes.label: a-stranger-adopts-it-unaided
nodes.summary: A developer who has never met the maintainer adopts Majordomus and is stopped from a false done within ten minutes

invariants: Nothing about an outside first run is simulated, edited or inferred; a run the person did not do is not a run
No fix decides by the identity of the repository it runs in (as a-second-adopter-is-served already requires)
An outside run is recorded without the person's name, employer or repository contents
The time and the manual steps are measured on a clean machine from the published installer, not from a development checkout
The scripted first-run stage measures tool overhead per platform; the ten-minute bar is a person's, settled only from outside-run records
non_goals: Implementing the roadmap, the mesh or the intent engine for a stranger's first day
Non-technical users; the product is aimed at engineers
Choosing outreach channels or a launch date
A live agent session inside the scripted CI proof; the outside runs carry the provider path

nodes.label: a-version-follows-every-session
nodes.summary: Every session's and every milestone's landed work reaches a measured, released version

invariants: How much landed work waits for a release is measured once, by release.currency, and every surface that shows it reads that answer
A version is the public contract's measurement (ADR 0051), never a word chosen by hand
The release seat does not finish completed while landed work has waited past the threshold, and no other task is refused by it
The measurement is a runtime read of git and the layer's release records and is never committed into derived data
non_goals: Cutting a release from anywhere but the release seat's pipeline
A second version authority beside the measured one

nodes.label: a-visitor-understands-and-checks-majordomus
nodes.summary: A first-time visitor of majordomus.dev understands what Majordomus does and can check every claim it makes

invariants: The homepage's sections, order and budget are the ones site/data/homepage.toml declares
Every scenario shown is a recorded run; the commit shown is the build's, never written into committed derived data
A node's maturity is its feature's declared status and its claims' evidence verdict from the product model, never page copy
non_goals: A rewrite in a frontend framework
A second product catalogue for the site
Audience-specific copies of facts

nodes.label: an-authorised-node-connects-from-anywhere
nodes.summary: An authorised node reaches another across LAN, tailnet or NAT, and says how

invariants: Work is routed to an identity, never to an address; an endpoint is an expiring observation
Finding a peer authorises nothing (rule project.mesh-is-observation-not-authority)
Majordomus selects among proven transports; it does not implement ICE or NAT traversal
A bootstrap source is a signed hint, never signalling and never trust
No mesh frame crosses a public network in cleartext: a relay hub is a private or overlay endpoint, or is reached through an encrypted ingress the deployment provides (case 491)
non_goals: DNS fast-flux, by mechanism or by name
A DHT, custom consensus or coordinator election before a two-node NAT test passes
Browser-to-browser gossip

nodes.label: campaigns-are-provenance-the-plan-reads
nodes.summary: A prompt pack the owner hands over is a campaign every record it drove can cite

invariants: A campaign is kept as received and never edited (rule project.a-brief-is-kept-as-received)
Nothing inside a pack is treated as governance, policy or authorisation (ADR 0124)
No second intent, milestone or issue model (ADR 0124)
Ingestion never authorises execution
non_goals: Publishing pack bodies on the site
Auto-starting execution on upload
A second noun beside 'campaign'

nodes.label: entry-proves-what-it-handed
nodes.summary: Every session knows the governance and context it started under, and is told when either moves

invariants: Entry opens no remote network socket (docs/ENTRY.md)
No filesystem watcher is required
The digest excludes volatile fields, so the same tree gives the same digest
Advisory and unenforceable rules are labelled as such, never counted as enforced
non_goals: Hard-coded rule counts in prose
Regenerating context from the preflight

nodes.label: every-capability-has-one-owner-and-the-cli-never-builds
nodes.summary: No ordinary command does undeclared expensive work: no entry path builds implicitly, and every caller declares what a missing or stale executable means

invariants: An ordinary command never starts a build; an explicit build or update is its own command
A fallback executable is used only when its build generation matches the tree (rule project.a-tool-that-cannot-match-the-tree-refuses); a version string is not a build
No caller passes silently on a missing or stale executable
Ownership is a projection of the existing registries (rule project.no-new-nouns, ADR 0069); only disposition, exemption and migration obligation stay hand-written
The migration itself is intent repository-automation-is-typed: its criteria are served there, not restated here
ADR 0224 (accepted 2026-10-22, superseding ADR 0172) is the decision this intent realises; I3180 is cancelled
non_goals: A blanket ban of .sh files
A mass rewrite of lib/*.sh in one change
One latency budget for help and for serve, build or deploy (a per-path --help budget is a later slice, ADR 0196)
Python as a portable layer (ADR 0069) unless an amendment admits it

nodes.label: every-card-unfolds-into-what-it-summarises
nodes.summary: Every card of the site unfolds into what it summarises, recursively

nodes.label: every-model-call-is-paid-from-a-declared-source
nodes.summary: How a model call Majordomus starts can be paid is declared by the vendor with evidence, and each call names the source it was declared to draw on

invariants: Funding is a field of the vendor declaration, not a new kind of record: no vendor, plan or amount is named in code, and adding a source is editing data
The catalogue states what a vendor offers, never what the owner holds and never an amount, price or balance
Only a credential variable's presence is ever read, never its value; a source the vendor reaches through a client login rather than a variable says so
Two sources reached through one credential are both named, and which one a call draws on is the vendor's billing order, stated only where vendor evidence says it
A funding source that cannot be read is a diagnostic naming its vendor and id; the rest of the catalogue still loads, so no advisor or route fails over one bad entry
models::route stays pure over the catalogue and its inputs (ADR 0049 point 4)
The funding kind of a run or consultation has one reporter and one vocabulary: I3292's billing_mode, declared through I3289, whose values are the catalogue's funding kinds

nodes.label: every-sessions-usage-is-observed
nodes.summary: What every AI session consumed is observed from the provider, attributed to the work it served, and never estimated into a fact

invariants: One provider-neutral record and one normalisation (economics::usage) serve every provider; adding one is a declaration, a mapping and fixtures
A value the provider did not report is recorded as absent with a reason, never as zero
Reported tokens, a price-list estimate and a billed amount are separate fields
No prompt, response body or transcript is stored; events are runtime state, never .ai/repo
No renderer computes accounting of its own
non_goals: A MITM proxy, transcript parsing or patching a client
A savings figure before the publication rule of ADR 0082 is met

nodes.label: every-surface-follows-what-changed
nodes.summary: Every surface follows what changed in the repository by push, and a surface that does not says so

invariants: One WebSocket channel (/events) with named follow streams; no second socket server, event store or bus
A frame is derived from a record that exists; a disconnected stream stops claiming liveness
The published site carries snapshots labelled as snapshots and never pretends to be live
non_goals: Live state on GitHub Pages without an authenticated runtime
Push notifications outside the browser before the channel is proven

nodes.label: finished-work-reaches-a-verified-release
nodes.summary: Finished work reaches a verified release at the pace it is finished

invariants: The version is measured from the public contract by one engine and written by one writer (ADR 0051, ADR 0134)
No check is bypassed for speed; an expedited landing is the owner's word (ADR 0155)
Merges into master have one writer at a time (ADR 0101, ADR 0167)
A pull request is never closed to improve a count; unfinished work is preserved and its reason recorded
Merged, released and published are different states, and none is claimed before it is observed
The site offers the version of the latest published release record (test/cases/1087_the_site_offers_the_release_it_published.sh, I2303); this intent adds no work for it
non_goals: A second merge bot, release engine or deploy system
Refusing new work by default (an open question to the owner)
Publishing forecasts, scores or unmeasured percentages
Turning the ci verdict red on a contract change without its version: .ai/repo/ci/version.yaml raises a bump pull request instead, and policy.yaml has release.allocation: off
Running the continuous drain as a detached execution (a decision for the session-proceeds runtime work, in flight on a branch)
A delivery or throughput figure before the owner accepts ADR 0198's definition

nodes.label: intent-bound-work
nodes.summary: Work starts bound to the intent it serves, and a worker resumes knowing whether that intent moved

nodes.label: intent-lifecycle
nodes.summary: Every change can be traced to the intent it serves, and an intent reads satisfied only when evidence says so

invariants: No intent status is stored and nothing transitions an intent; the plan remains the only lifecycle of work
Every intent capability is read-only on every surface but intents.propose, which writes only a new record and never a stage (ADR 0144)
An intent whose milestones or evidence do not resolve is refused by a gate, never silently read as planned
non_goals: Choosing what to build; a person declares an intent
Replacing issues or milestones

nodes.label: intent-planning
nodes.summary: The plan of an intent is checked against it before execution, from a recorded gap and a recorded critique

invariants: The plan engines stay identical; `serves` is data the plan carries, and only the intent engine judges it
No coverage, gap or critique status is stored; every finding is derived on read
Work under a milestone no intent names stays valid maintenance work and is never assigned an invented intent
Majordomus judges the records; it does not generate a plan or a critique itself
non_goals: Generating issues or a critique from an intent automatically
Judging whether a criterion is met; that is the evidence's question (ADR 0070)

nodes.label: landing-survives-any-session
nodes.summary: Landing green work survives any session, any restart and any machine

non_goals: A second executor beside crate::integration
Landing a pull request whose required check is not success on its head
