A threshold so tight that ordinary content growth fails the build
facts.objective: Measure what this architecture costs — discovery, reconciliation, the environment entry, the generated artifacts — and hold each to a budget derived from its measured baseline.
facts.risk: Wall-clock thresholds are noisy across machines. The structural counters gate strictly and the timings conservatively, as the existing performance doctrine already decided.
facts.why: A spine every consumer reads is a cost every consumer pays. Measured once and then never again, it grows until somebody works around the tool instead of using it.

nodes.label: I1120
nodes.summary: A refusal says what to do about it

acceptance_criteria: A refusal names the file or path, what was found, what was expected and the command that repairs it
An edited bridge, a ledger mismatch, a non-conforming path and a plan touching something unowned each have their own message rather than a shared generic one
The messages are exercised by tests, so a change that degrades one is caught
Machine-readable output carries the same detail as the human-readable form
facts.current_state: Errors in the executable carry structured detail in places and a bare message in others. The new operations have no convention yet.
facts.desired_state: Each refusal is actionable, and a person who has never read this code can act on it without reading this code.
non_scope: A second diagnostics framework
A message that reports a condition without naming the repair
facts.objective: Make every refusal in this subsystem name the source of truth, what was observed, what was expected and the command that repairs it — through the diagnostics framework that already exists.
facts.risk: Message quality is the first thing to decay under time pressure and the last thing anybody tests. Testing the messages is what keeps them.

nodes.label: I1121
nodes.summary: Every surface shows the integration from the one model

acceptance_criteria: The integration reads are declared once and appear in the CLI, the API, the API document, MCP, the Cockpit and the generated reference with no second registration
No mutating operation is exposed to an untrusted surface; adoption and removal stay with the trusted command line
The Cockpit shows what is adopted, what is owned and what a reconciliation would change, from that declaration
The published documentation derives its integration reference from the same model, with no retyped value
facts.current_state: The capability registry already projects declared operations into every surface. The integration state is not among them.
facts.desired_state: One declaration exposes the integration reads, and every surface derives from it as it does for everything else.
non_scope: A mutating integration operation exposed to unauthenticated HTTP or to a browser
A hand-edited API document, route table or documentation list
facts.risk: Showing what a reconciliation would change means running the plan on a request. Its cost belongs to the budget, and a read that builds a plan has to say so.
facts.why: The question a person asks about an integration is what it did to my repository, and they will ask it wherever they happen to be. Answering it four ways is how the four answers begin to differ.

nodes.label: I1122
nodes.summary: A foreign repository, adopted, upgraded and given back

acceptance_criteria: Adoption of a repository with no prior Majordomus state adds the two namespaces and the declared bridges, and nothing else, verified against the tree rather than against the report
The second adoption changes nothing
An adoption made by an older version reconciles forward without rewriting a bridge that did not need to change
A bridge edited by a person is refused rather than overwritten, and reported
Removal returns the repository to what it was, apart from authored content, compared against a recorded starting state
The fixture is ordinary in every respect and nothing in the implementation recognises it
facts.current_state: Nothing has been adopted anywhere but here.
facts.desired_state: One test drives the whole lifecycle on a foreign fixture and asserts each stage, including the ones designed to refuse.
non_scope: A fixture the implementation recognises as a test
Declaring success from the exit code of an adoption
facts.risk: An end-to-end test with a fixture the implementation special-cases proves nothing. The fixture has to be indistinguishable from a real repository.

nodes.label: I1123
nodes.summary: The milestone is accepted on its evidence

acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion of the milestone has evidence recorded against it
The measured footprint of an adoption is recorded — every path, with its namespace and its owner
The budgets are recorded with the machine and environment they were measured on
The documented adoption and removal run exactly as written on a clean checkout
Pre-existing failures, failures introduced here and failures fixed here are distinguished explicitly
Remaining limitations are stated rather than omitted
facts.current_state: Open.
facts.desired_state: Accepted with evidence against every criterion, with the footprint, the budgets and the limitations written where they will be found.
non_scope: Reporting a mechanism as proved without the artifact that proves it
facts.risk: The end of a long milestone is where intent gets recorded as outcome. Anything not demonstrated is written as a limitation.
facts.why: A milestone is accepted by its evidence. What a later reader has is the record, not this session.

nodes.label: I1201
nodes.summary: An identity provider is a declarative object, and Google and Facebook are two of them

acceptance_criteria: The schema expresses one flow shape, and both objects validate against it without a per-provider escape hatch
Credentials are named, never carried: each object states the environment variable names and holds no value
The directory satisfies the recursive README and front-matter doctrine of the layer
The allow-list is generated from the schema by majordomus generate rather than written by hand
majordomus doctor reports the new kind and both objects with no diagnostic
facts.current_state: There is no identity kind, no .ai/repo/identity directory and no notion of a provider anywhere in the layer or the executable.
non_scope: Any Rust code that reads the objects, which is I1202
A client secret, a client id or any credential value in any file of the repository
A provider-specific field that only one of the two objects can use

nodes.label: I1202
nodes.summary: One typed provider model reads the objects, and no code names a provider

acceptance_criteria: The provider set is discovered from the directory, validated, and ordered deterministically
A provider with absent credentials is unavailable with a stated reason, and the reason reaches the surfaces
No provider identifier appears in the executable's source outside test fixtures
The read is declared once as a capability and appears in CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and docs with no second registration
facts.current_state: I1201 has the objects; nothing reads them.
non_scope: The HTTP flow, which is I1203
Reading a credential value into any type that is serialised, cached, logged or rendered
facts.risk: Resolving credentials at load makes the model unusable in any context that serialises it. They are resolved at the moment of the flow and never held.

nodes.label: I1203
nodes.summary: One flow serves every provider, and it refuses everything it did not start

acceptance_criteria: State and nonce are single-use, expiring, and bound to the provider they were issued for
The identity token is verified for issuer, audience, expiry and nonce before any session exists
A callback whose state was not issued by this server is refused without a session and without a redirect that leaks the parameters
The redirect target after sign-in is validated against the surface's own origin rather than taken from the request
Every refusal path has a test, and the tests run without contacting either provider
facts.current_state: I1202 gives the providers; there is no flow, no route and no verification.
non_scope: Storing anything about the reader beyond the session of I1204
A provider-specific branch anywhere in the flow
facts.risk: An open redirect and an unvalidated state are the two classic defects of this flow. Both are tested as refusals rather than assumed.

nodes.label: I1204
nodes.summary: The session is signed, short, and revocable from the server

acceptance_criteria: The cookie is signed with a key that comes from the environment and is absent from every artifact
Secure is set whenever the surface is served over anything but loopback, and the decision comes from the surface rather than from a constant
Sign-out revokes server-side, and a revoked session is refused even if the cookie is replayed
Expiry is enforced on the server, not only in the cookie's attributes
facts.current_state: No cookie, no session, no signing key handling.
facts.desired_state: A session exists as long as it is meant to, survives a restart only if that is the stated decision, and is gone from the server the moment sign-out is called.
non_scope: A session store shared between deployments
Remembering anything about the reader between sessions
facts.risk: A signing key with a compiled-in default is a signing key that ships. Its absence is a refusal to issue sessions, not a fallback.
facts.why: A cookie that only the browser can invalidate cannot be signed out of, and a session that carries claims in its payload cannot be revoked when the provider set changes underneath it.

nodes.label: I1205
nodes.summary: Identity is resolved once, in the router, and every surface reads it from there

acceptance_criteria: Exactly one place reads the session cookie, proved by a test that fails when a second appears
The Cockpit shows who is signed in and offers sign-out, from the resolved caller rather than from its own read
The MCP surface receives the same caller as the HTTP API for the same connection
An anonymous caller is a value, not an absence, so no surface can forget to handle it
facts.current_state: I1204 issues sessions; nothing reads them outside the flow.
facts.desired_state: A request carries a resolved caller — anonymous or identified — from the router onward, and a handler cannot be written that skips the resolution.
non_scope: Roles, groups or permissions beyond identified and anonymous
A second resolution in any surface
facts.risk: The Cockpit is the surface most likely to re-read the cookie for convenience. The test that forbids a second read is what keeps it honest.

nodes.label: I1206
nodes.summary: What an anonymous reader may do is derived from the effect classification, not from a list

acceptance_criteria: The policy states the requirement per effect class, and no route names its own requirement
A capability added with a mutating effect is refused to an anonymous caller with no edit to the HTTP layer, proved by a test capability
The OpenAPI document carries the security scheme and marks the operations that require it, generated rather than written
The Cockpit disables what the caller may not invoke and states the reason it is disabled
facts.current_state: Every route is served to everyone; the fly-deployment milestone therefore forbids exposing any mutating operation to the browser.
facts.desired_state: Adding a capability inherits its exposure from its effect class, and a capability that mutates cannot be reached anonymously without a policy change that is visible as one.
non_scope: A per-route authorisation table in any format
Granting a signed-in reader anything the effect policy has not classified
facts.risk: This issue depends on the effect classification being trustworthy. Where a capability's class is wrong, the fix is the classification, never an exception in the router.

nodes.label: I1207
nodes.summary: No credential reaches any output, and hostile provider metadata renders safely

acceptance_criteria: The sentinel sweep covers every output surface the repository produces, enumerated from the registry rather than listed by hand where that is possible
A deliberate regression that renders a secret is caught by the test, proved by a negative case
Hostile provider metadata renders as text on every surface, with no escape and no truncation that hides it
The gate runs in CI on every change
facts.current_state: No credentials exist yet, so no test can leak one.
facts.desired_state: A sentinel test runs in CI and fails loudly if any future change routes a credential into an output.
non_scope: Weakening the assertion to the outputs that happen to pass today
facts.risk: A sweep that enumerates outputs by hand will miss the surface added after it. Where the registry can enumerate them, it does.
facts.why: Every other guarantee of this milestone is a claim until a test tries to break it, and a credential that leaks once has leaked permanently.

nodes.label: I1208
nodes.summary: Adding a provider is one file, removing one is one deletion, and both are executed rather than described

acceptance_criteria: A synthetic provider dropped into the directory appears on every applicable surface with no source edit, proved by a test
Removing a provider object removes it from every surface, and sessions pinned to that issuer are refused
The documentation names the file to write and the file to delete, and cites the tests that execute both
A rule states that a provider fact may not be stated outside its object, with a check CI executes
facts.current_state: Nothing is documented and nothing performs the lifecycle.
facts.desired_state: The add and the remove are both proved by tests, and the documentation states the one-file operation because a test executes it.
non_scope: A migration path for sessions issued by a provider that has been struck, beyond revoking them
facts.risk: The removal half is the half that is skipped, and it is the half the operator asked for.

nodes.label: I1301
nodes.summary: A workspace is a declared object of the layer; only its content is local

acceptance_criteria: The object states vendor, upstream workspace identity, display name, the authorisation the operator asserts, the browser profile reference by name, and the expected capability set
Keys are closed by share/allow/workspace.txt and an unknown key is refused
The directory carries a context README stating what is authoritative and what is generated, per ADR 0011
The object is listed and read through the existing object surface with no code that special-cases it
No secret value and no credential name appears in the object or its schema
facts.current_state: No workspace kind, no .ai/repo/workspaces directory, no allow file and no schema exist.
non_scope: Any synced content; the store is I1303
Any credential, cookie or token value; the declaration names a profile, it does not hold one
Any Rust that special-cases the kind
facts.risk: A schema written for ChatGPT becomes a ChatGPT file with a generic name. It has to state only what a second vendor would plausibly restate, and push everything else into a named vendor block.

nodes.label: I1302
nodes.summary: Identity, provenance and support level are typed fields, not prose

acceptance_criteria: A local identity is reproducible from vendor and upstream identity alone and never depends on a display title
Every record states its transport, its acquisition mode and its support level as enumerated values
A content hash distinguishes a changed record from a re-observed one
A record gone upstream is tombstoned with a stamp, never removed silently
The schema carries a version and an unknown version is refused rather than parsed
facts.current_state: Nothing exists. The repository's own kinds compute identity generically from declared fields (index.rs identity_of) and that mechanism does not reach local content.
facts.risk: Over-modelling. The enumerations must be the ones a consumer actually branches on; a taxonomy nobody reads is a cost with no reader.

nodes.label: I1303
nodes.summary: The store is bounded, measured and invisible to every published projection

acceptance_criteria: The store layout and the checkpoint are described by a schema, not by a comment
A retention cap is stated in policy.yaml and doctor reports the store against it, in the shape the three existing stanzas use
A gate fails if the site build, the generated documentation or any published projection names a path under .ai/local/workspaces/
A test case proves the gate fails when the boundary is crossed deliberately
facts.current_state: No store, no cap, no stanza. .ai/local/ is git-ignored at .gitignore:55 and mj_validate_ai_layout fails the pre-commit hook if a file there is tracked.
non_scope: Declaring the store as a knowledge-sources class; ADR 0025 rejected it and the reasons are recorded there
Any adapter that writes into the store
facts.objective: Declare the layout of .ai/local/workspaces/, its checkpoint file, its retention cap in policy and the doctor stanza that measures it, and prove with a gate that nothing published ever reaches it.
facts.risk: A cap chosen from taste rather than measurement will either never fire or fire on the first real sync. It has to be stated in terms of what the operator's own workspace actually holds.

nodes.label: I1304
nodes.summary: The browser transport is the one this repository already drives

acceptance_criteria: The transport attaches to an explicitly configured, already-authenticated browser profile and refuses to guess one
Observation is scoped to the origins the workspace declaration names; traffic to any other origin is never recorded
Authorisation headers, cookies and set-cookie values are redacted before an observation is written anywhere
The existing UI and cockpit consumers use the same launcher, so the repository has one answer to how it starts a browser
Absent Chrome or absent node_modules, the command skips with the defined exit code the repository already uses rather than failing
facts.current_state: The two existing consumers each inline their own chromium.launch; no shared launcher was factored out. Neither targets an authenticated third-party session.
non_scope: Any credential written to disk, including a copied cookie jar or a profile archive
Any interaction with authentication, multi-factor prompts or anti-abuse controls
DOM scraping where a network observation answers the same question

nodes.label: I1305
nodes.summary: An observed contract has a fingerprint, a compatibility state and a fixture

acceptance_criteria: Every observed operation has a fingerprint over its shape and a compatibility state
A mismatched shape fails closed; nothing partial is persisted
A degraded contract falls back to the browser transport where one exists, and reports unavailability where none does
Fixtures are sanitised at capture time and CI replays them with no network and no account
Promoting a new contract requires a person and a passing test, and the mechanism cannot do it alone
facts.current_state: Nothing exists.
non_scope: Hardcoding any endpoint path taken from a prompt, a gist or documentation rather than from observed authorised traffic
Automatic promotion of a new observed shape
facts.risk: A fixture is a recording of private conversation. Sanitisation that runs after capture is sanitisation that has already failed; it runs before anything reaches disk.
facts.why: A vendor's undocumented surface is not a contract and will change. The failure this must prevent is not the loud one; it is a parse that half succeeds and writes plausible nonsense into the store.

nodes.label: I1306
nodes.summary: A sync resumes, repeats itself without harm, and says how fresh it is

acceptance_criteria: A second run over an unchanged workspace leaves the store byte-identical
An interrupted run resumes from its checkpoint without re-fetching what it already had
Every change records the acquisition mode that produced it, and a poll is never reported as a push
A run is bounded by count and by wall clock and says what it did not reach
Replaying a captured run over fixtures reproduces the same store
facts.current_state: Nothing exists.
non_scope: Any write to the vendor
Watch semantics that call polling a subscription
facts.objective: Implement the sync: incremental from a durable checkpoint, idempotent on replay, bounded in what one run may fetch, and honest about how each change was acquired.

nodes.label: I1307
nodes.summary: The ChatGPT shape is mapped from evidence and never becomes the canonical model

acceptance_criteria: No vendor DTO field reaches the store or a capability without passing through the mapper
A branched conversation keeps its graph; no branch is silently dropped or linearised
Content parts keep a typed discriminator rather than being concatenated into text
A field the evidence does not support is absent rather than defaulted
The mapper is proven against sanitised fixtures with no live account
facts.current_state: Nothing exists. No observation has been taken.
non_scope: Any canonical field invented to match a vendor field with no consumer
Downloading attachment content where the declaration does not authorise it
facts.risk: Mapping ahead of evidence. Every field here must point at an observation that was actually taken, or it is a guess with a schema around it.

nodes.label: I1308
nodes.summary: The executable's share is one capability, shaped like continuity

acceptance_criteria: The capability is declared once and reaches CLI, HTTP and MCP through the existing registry with no second registration
No generated document, site dataset or published projection carries workspace content
A missing store is reported as absent, not as an empty success
majordomus-cli gains no dependency
facts.current_state: No capability reads .ai/local/workspaces/. continuity reads .ai/local/state/ and is the model to follow.
non_scope: Any new dependency in majordomus-cli; ADR 0025 forbids it and I1309 gates it
Any site, docs/generated or public projection of workspace content
Serving conversation bodies over HTTP before a person has decided that is wanted
facts.risk: The registry makes surfaces cheap, which is exactly the hazard here. The default for this capability is the narrowest exposure that answers the question, and widening it is a separate decision.

nodes.label: I1309
nodes.summary: The boundaries this milestone asserts are gates, not sentences

acceptance_criteria: A gate fails if majordomus-cli's runtime dependency list changes, naming what was added
A gate greps the store, the fixtures, the logs and the snapshots for credential-shaped values and fails on a hit
A gate fails if the store exceeds its declared retention cap
A gate fails if any published projection names a path under .ai/local/workspaces/
Each gate has a test case that proves it red before it proves it green, and each rule carries the x-majordomus block that makes it enforced rather than stated
facts.current_state: No gate covers any of them. The only adjacent precedent is scripts/site-check, which greps rendered output for secret-shaped strings and fails the site gate.
facts.desired_state: Four gates in .ai/repo/ci/gates.yaml, each a script, each selected by the paths it protects, each with a test case that proves it fails when the boundary is crossed.
non_scope: Adding a new CI job; these gates belong to jobs that already exist
facts.objective: Add the gates that make ADR 0025 enforceable: the dependency boundary of majordomus-cli, the credential leak check over the store and the fixtures, the retention cap, and the publication boundary.
facts.risk: A leak grep tuned to today's token shapes finds today's tokens. It is a floor, and the record says so rather than implying the boundary is proven.

nodes.label: I1310
nodes.summary: The subsystem is documented where a person looks, and the plan is closed against the repository

acceptance_criteria: docs/WORKSPACES.md exists, is linked from the documentation index, and renders on the site
The document states the distinction from ADR 0024's provider in its own words, so that a reader who never opens the ADR does not conflate them
The re-audit names every place a second implementation of an existing mechanism was avoided, and every place one survives
ADR 0025 is accepted or amended by a person, and its status reflects what was actually built
facts.current_state: ADR 0025 records the decision and its withdrawal of two earlier positions. Nothing in docs/ describes the subsystem.
non_scope: Documenting a capability that does not exist yet
facts.risk: Documentation written from the plan rather than from the built subsystem. It is written last for that reason.

nodes.label: I1401
nodes.summary: The identity of a projected record is what the record carries, not what its title says

acceptance_criteria: A record is resolved by the identity it carries, and a renamed title neither loses it nor duplicates it
An issue carrying no identity marker is adopted by its title once, reported as an adoption, and given a marker by --apply
A title that merely looks canonical never captures a record that carries a different identity
A created issue takes its number from the creation, with no title search anywhere in the adapter
Reconciliation is provable against a fixture remote with no network and no token, and a fixture is refused for --apply
non_scope: Writing a GitHub number into a canonical record
Any change to what the projection renders
facts.risk: The 19 issues projected before the marker existed must be adopted, never re-created; the adoption path is the acceptance criterion that guards it.

nodes.label: I1402
nodes.summary: A finding says which of six states it found, and the state that could hide a person's edit is no longer one of them

acceptance_criteria: A person's edit is detected whether or not the canonical record has moved since, proved by a case for each
A record whose region was edited and whose canonical record also moved is reported as conflict, and --apply refuses it without --force
An issue claiming a canonical id this repository does not have is reported and counted, so --check fails on it
Every state is proved by a case that builds the remote as a fixture, offline
facts.risk: Low. Every distinction is derived from bytes both sides already carry.

nodes.label: I1403
nodes.summary: Backfill the projection once, deliberately, and record what it created

acceptance_criteria: The dry run is read and its counts agree with the check before anything is applied
The 19 existing issues are adopted, not duplicated, and the issue count after the run equals the canonical count
scripts/github-sync --check exits 0 immediately after the run
The gate's baseline is lowered to zero in the same commit, so the backlog cannot silently return
The run is recorded as evidence naming the date, the counts and the commit
facts.desired_state: `scripts/github-sync --check` exits 0. Every canonical record holds the number it was projected onto. The run is recorded as evidence with its date and the count it created.
non_scope: Any change to the adapter, which I1401 and I1402 own
Closing or reopening a GitHub issue by hand
facts.objective: Apply the projection so that every canonical record exists on GitHub exactly once, adopt the 19 records that already exist rather than duplicating them, and record the run as evidence.

nodes.label: I1404
nodes.summary: The drift check is a gate, so a projection that stops being applied cannot stay silent

facts.desired_state: A drift finding is a build failure. The gate needs a token to read the remote, so it declares what it needs and says so when it is absent rather than passing quietly.
non_scope: Applying the projection from CI, which stays a deliberate human act
facts.objective: Run `scripts/github-sync --check` from CI on every change that can move the canonical model or the adapter, and fail the build on drift with the record and the remedy named.

nodes.label: I1405
nodes.summary: A pull request names the issue it realises, and the edge is derived rather than remembered

acceptance_criteria: Given an issue id, the branches, commits and pull requests that realised it are listed, derived from git and GitHub
Given a commit or a pull request, the issue and the milestone it served are named, or it is reported as unattributed
Work with no execution contract is reported as unattributed rather than silently omitted
The derivation reads no stored edge that git or GitHub already holds
non_scope: Requiring a branch to encode an issue id where doctrine does not already require it
Storing a commit list in a canonical record; git owns commits
facts.objective: Derive the relation between an issue and the pull requests, branches and commits that realised it, from git and from GitHub, and make it traversable in both directions.
facts.risk: A commit-to-issue edge inferred from a branch name is only as good as the branch discipline; unattributed must be a reported state, not an assumption.

nodes.label: I1406
nodes.summary: The plan's derivations are capabilities, so every surface reads the readiness the terminal reads

acceptance_criteria: The derivations are declared once and projected to MCP, HTTP and OpenAPI with no transport registry edited by hand
The executable and the shell answer identically for every record in this repository, proved by a test that compares them
majordomus generate --check is clean after the declaration is added
The Cockpit shows the derived plan and its drift
non_scope: Changing what the derivations mean
A second plan implementation that may disagree with the first
facts.objective: Make status, ready, blocked, waves, next and roadmap answerable through the capability registry, so that MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI and the Cockpit read the derived plan rather than only the raw documents.
facts.risk: Two implementations of one derivation is the failure this repository exists to prevent; the equality test is the acceptance criterion, not a nicety.

nodes.label: I1407
nodes.summary: One issue travels the whole path and back, as an executable case

facts.statement: Every reusable prompt asset renders, and every token in it is one the renderer knows.

nodes.label: majordomus.publication-currency@1
nodes.summary: A session does not finish behind its own published site

nodes.label: majordomus.questions-store-integrity@1
nodes.summary: Questions store integrity

facts.statement: Every entry in the questions store parses, because a gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one.

nodes.label: majordomus.record-changed-files@1
nodes.summary: A record's changed_files names the work, not the tool's exhaust

nodes.label: majordomus.retention-caps@1
nodes.summary: Retention caps

facts.statement: The ledger, the handovers, the checkpoints and the session records stay under the caps the policy sets, and a cap is met by moving records aside, never by deleting one.

nodes.label: majordomus.roadmap-integrity@1
nodes.summary: The roadmap is a projection, never a document

nodes.label: majordomus.rule-package-integrity@1
nodes.summary: Rule package integrity

facts.statement: The vendored baseline matches its manifest file for file, every effective rule resolves with its dependencies, no two rules claim one identity, and no project rule reuses the vendored namespace.

nodes.label: majordomus.schema-integrity@1
nodes.summary: Every object has a schema, and the rules resolve in one stated order

nodes.label: majordomus.scope-integrity@1
nodes.summary: Scope integrity

facts.statement: Work outside the paths a task claimed is not accepted as that task's work.

nodes.label: majordomus.session-lifecycle@1
nodes.summary: The episode boundary is drawn below the model, and its working context is local

nodes.label: majordomus.session-records@1
nodes.summary: Session records are shared objects with a closed field set

nodes.label: majordomus.sessions-are-workers@1
nodes.summary: Sessions are workers, not memory

facts.statement: Treat every session as a worker that reads state from records and writes state to records; nothing that only a conversation remembers is state.

nodes.label: majordomus.skill-integrity@1
nodes.summary: Skill integrity

nodes.label: majordomus.state-consistency@1
nodes.summary: State consistency

facts.statement: A task record is trusted only while it still describes this checkout: same branch, HEAD at or ahead of the recorded commit.

nodes.label: majordomus.task-continuity@1
nodes.summary: Task continuity

facts.statement: A task finished as partial or blocked leaves a handover record, not only a note section.

nodes.label: majordomus.task-on-the-mesh@1
nodes.summary: A task on a repository whose mesh is enabled works on the mesh

nodes.label: majordomus.use-case-coverage@1
nodes.summary: Use-case coverage

facts.statement: A capability the policy requires coverage for is demonstrated by an executable use case, and a capability without one is a named gap.

nodes.label: majordomus.verification-integrity@1
nodes.summary: Verification integrity

nodes.label: majordomus.verify-outcomes@1
nodes.summary: Verify outcomes, not activity

facts.statement: Accept a verification command's recorded exit code as evidence of completion, and accept nothing that merely describes verification.

nodes.label: project.a-brief-is-kept-as-received@1
nodes.summary: A campaign brief this repository keeps is the one it was handed

facts.statement: Keep a campaign brief as it was received, record its bytes in the manifest and its pack in the index, and let the repository rather than the brief say what came of it.

nodes.label: project.a-build-never-waits-in-silence-on-anothers-lock@1
nodes.summary: A build never waits in silence behind another build's lock

nodes.label: project.a-checkout-serves-the-current-trunk@1
nodes.summary: A checkout serves the current trunk, and says how far it is from it

nodes.label: project.a-closing-question-is-answered-by-measurement@1
nodes.summary: Whether the work is done is answered by measurement, never by the worker's recollection

nodes.label: project.a-derive-offload-waits-its-turn@1
nodes.summary: A derive offloaded to another machine goes through the declared hosts and waits its turn in their queue

nodes.label: project.a-derive-sees-what-the-commit-will@1
nodes.summary: A derive sees what the commit will

facts.statement: Stage every new file before you derive, and ignore or remove what will never be committed. scripts/derive refuses an untracked, non-ignored file before it takes the machine's lock and names each one.

nodes.label: project.a-diagram-is-drawn-not-typed@2
nodes.summary: An architectural relationship in a published document is drawn, never typed in box art

nodes.label: project.a-failed-read-is-not-an-empty-answer@1
nodes.summary: A source that did not answer is not a source with nothing in it

nodes.label: project.a-number-names-one-case@1
nodes.summary: A case number names one case

nodes.label: project.a-personal-layer-changes-nothing-shared@1
nodes.summary: A personal layer changes nothing shared

nodes.label: project.a-plan-carries-the-intent-it-serves@1
nodes.summary: A plan carries the intent it serves, and is reviewed before it is executed

nodes.label: project.a-producer-declares-what-it-writes@1
nodes.summary: The program that writes into the checkout says what it wrote, and whoever measures the tree reads that

nodes.label: project.a-provider-capability-cites-its-evidence@3
nodes.summary: A provider capability is declared once, with the citation it was verified from

nodes.label: project.a-push-runs-what-ci-would-find-first@2
nodes.summary: A push runs what CI would find first, and CI decides

nodes.label: project.a-session-joins-the-cluster-before-it-works@1
nodes.summary: A session is current, attached, announced and useful before it changes anything

nodes.label: project.a-standing-approval-is-written-where-permissions-are-read@1
nodes.summary: A standing approval is written where the permission layer reads it

nodes.label: project.a-tool-that-cannot-match-the-tree-refuses@1
nodes.summary: A generator that cannot match the tree refuses rather than rewriting it

facts.statement: A generator whose build does not match the tree it is asked to derive refuses, names both sides, and exits non-zero; it never writes.

nodes.label: project.a-verdict-states-its-subject@1
nodes.summary: A verdict states what it is a verdict about

facts.statement: A verdict names its denominator, and a detector distinguishes its subject from what merely looks like its subject.

nodes.label: project.a-worker-that-stops-leaves-its-work-behind@2
nodes.summary: A worker that stops leaves its work where somebody else can find it

nodes.label: project.accumulation-is-measured@2
nodes.summary: Everything that accumulates is measured, bounded and reaped by a committed command

nodes.label: project.advisors-are-optional@1
nodes.summary: Advisors are optional; reasoning, governance and CI never depend on one

facts.statement: Name advisory capabilities, never advisors, in reasoning code; derive availability from presence and recorded outcomes; treat no advisor as an ordinary plan; and keep every model credential out of CI.

nodes.label: project.an-exclusive-claim-lives-by-its-holders-progress@1
nodes.summary: An exclusive mesh claim lives by its holder session's progress, not only by its runtime's beat

nodes.label: project.an-expedited-landing-is-the-owners-word@1
nodes.summary: An expedited landing is the owner's word, judged on the merged tree, and never reaches a tag

nodes.label: project.an-intent-outlives-its-sessions@3
nodes.summary: An intent outlives the sessions and providers that realise it, and closed work does not outrank evidence

nodes.label: project.benchmarkable-commands@1
nodes.summary: Every public command is benchmarkable from the registry

nodes.label: project.blocking-checks-cheap@1
nodes.summary: Blocking checks are deterministic and cheap

facts.statement: A check that can stop a command is deterministic and cheap; work in progress is reported, never blocked.

nodes.label: project.cache-is-invisible@2
nodes.summary: A cache never changes what a command observes

nodes.label: project.canonical-order@1
nodes.summary: A collection has one order, owned by one place, and it does not depend on who ran the command

nodes.label: project.clean-room@1
nodes.summary: Clean room

facts.statement: The Prismatic name is the only thing carried from anywhere else: no internal paths, hostnames, component names, doctrine vocabulary or quotations.

nodes.label: project.commands-are-projections@1
nodes.summary: A command is declared once, and every surface that shows it is a projection

nodes.label: project.commands-run-non-interactively@2
nodes.summary: A command runs with nobody at the keyboard

facts.statement: Where a non-interactive form exists it is the one used; a command that can block for input is not run unless the operator asked for an interactive session.

nodes.label: project.completion-never-decides-satisfaction@2
nodes.summary: Completion discharges obligations and never decides whether an intent is satisfied

nodes.label: project.context-locality@1
nodes.summary: Context locality

facts.statement: Context lives in the narrowest directory scope where it stays correct; root files bootstrap and link; provider files are projections.

nodes.label: project.conventional-commits@2
nodes.summary: A commit message is a value this repository judges, not a convention it hopes for

nodes.label: project.derived-files-regenerated@1
nodes.summary: Derived files are regenerated, never edited

facts.statement: A generated file is changed by changing its canonical source and rerunning the generator, and both are committed together; the fingerprint gate refuses the commit that does not.

nodes.label: project.derived-once@1
nodes.summary: Derived state is computed once per state version

facts.statement: Compute canonical truth once per state version, project it once where possible, execute only what is request-specific, and prove it with the work counters rather than with a clock.

nodes.label: project.design-tokens-declared-once@2
nodes.summary: The design is one typed declaration and every first-party surface consumes its projections

nodes.label: project.destructive-sweeps-fail-closed@1
nodes.summary: A sweep that deletes fails closed on what it could not read

nodes.label: project.development-semantics-are-canonical@1
nodes.summary: Development semantics live in the canonical runtime; a surface only consumes them

nodes.label: project.diagnostics-decide-the-exit@1
nodes.summary: A return code is not the diagnostic channel

nodes.label: project.distribution-canonical@1
nodes.summary: Distribution has one canonical model

nodes.label: project.empty-is-not-failure@1
nodes.summary: An empty result and a failed command must not look alike

facts.statement: Distinguish "there is nothing" from "I could not look", at every boundary where one program reads another's output, and make the second one say so.

nodes.label: project.english-only@4
nodes.summary: English only

nodes.label: project.entities-are-routable@1
nodes.summary: Every object of the layer has an address of its own, and every kind says where it is published

nodes.label: project.entry-converges@2
nodes.summary: Entering the repository converges on a server, by either door, without anything to remember

nodes.label: project.entry-reports-only-evidence@1
nodes.summary: Entering the repository reports only what evidence proves

nodes.label: project.envrc-is-an-adapter@2
nodes.summary: The shell entry point is an adapter, and it makes one call

nodes.label: project.episode-record-carries-its-episode@1
nodes.summary: An episode record carries its episode

nodes.label: project.every-domain-is-a-skill@1
nodes.summary: Every domain of the registry is a skill, derived and shown wherever skills are

facts.statement: A skill an agent reads is derived from the registry or the layer's skills section, never written by hand, and every surface that lists skills reads the one projection that derives them.

nodes.label: project.every-link-and-control-is-tested@1
nodes.summary: Every link the site publishes resolves, and every control on it does what a spec says

nodes.label: project.every-wait-is-bounded@2
nodes.summary: Every wait is bounded

facts.statement: A wait without a timeout, a completion predicate and a recovery path is not a wait but a hang; silence is inspected, never counted as progress.

nodes.label: project.execution-events-are-typed@1
nodes.summary: A long operation reports typed events, and a transport only renders them

nodes.label: project.execution-state-is-authoritative@1
nodes.summary: Execution state is authoritative and the terminal is not

nodes.label: project.executions-carry-no-secret@1
nodes.summary: A sensitive value never enters an execution

facts.statement: Redact from the schema, once, before the value is stored; never from a field's name, never a second time in a transport, and never in a page.

nodes.label: project.finding-carries-reproduce@1
nodes.summary: Every finding carries a reproduce command

facts.statement: Every finding a command reports names the command that reproduces it.

nodes.label: project.generated-artifacts-are-typed@1
nodes.summary: A generated artifact declares its document, its encoding, its contract and its source

nodes.label: project.github-projection-gated@1
nodes.summary: The GitHub projection is checked by a gate, not by somebody remembering to run it

nodes.label: project.homepage-tells-a-declared-story@2
nodes.summary: The homepage tells the story its declaration names, in that order, and the site is indexed by one declared policy

nodes.label: project.hot-path-reads-once@1
nodes.summary: A command reads each canonical file at most once

facts.statement: One invocation, one reading per canonical file; the work counters are the proof, and a count that exceeds the number of distinct files read is a defect.

nodes.label: project.independent-of-prismatic@1
nodes.summary: Independent of Prismatic

nodes.label: project.integration-follows-the-current-master@3
nodes.summary: Pull requests are integrated one at a time, each decided against the current master, never around the branch protection

nodes.label: project.interfaces-are-projections@1
nodes.summary: External interfaces are projections of one capability definition

facts.statement: A capability is defined once and every external interface is derived from that definition; an interface that carries a definition of its own is a bug.

nodes.label: project.land-and-publish@1
nodes.summary: Work lands often and small, and what is published is master and only master

nodes.label: project.mesh-cooperation-is-authenticated@1
nodes.summary: Mesh cooperation is admitted per link, replicated through one journal, and projected by every surface alike

nodes.label: project.mesh-is-observation-not-authority@1
nodes.summary: The mesh observes nodes; it authorizes nothing and holds one registry

nodes.label: project.native-cli-documented@1
nodes.summary: A native command line command exists only with its documentation and its executable examples

nodes.label: project.navigation-is-declared-once@1
nodes.summary: The site's navigation is declared once, and every projection derives from that declaration

nodes.label: project.never-author-identity@1
nodes.summary: Never author identity fields

facts.statement: repository_id, branch, head, working_tree and changed_files on any record are computed from git and never written by hand.

nodes.label: project.never-reported-is-not-green@1
nodes.summary: A verdict that never arrived is not a verdict

facts.statement: A check that has not reported is unknown, never passing; a change is merged against the trunk's measured failing set, not against silence.

nodes.label: project.never-store-transcripts@1
nodes.summary: Never store or summarise transcripts

facts.statement: No record stores or summarises a conversation; records carry what is true now and the next action.

nodes.label: project.new-code-is-covered@1
nodes.summary: New and changed executable code is covered by a test; legacy debt may only shrink

nodes.label: project.no-claim-without-test@1
nodes.summary: No claim without a test

facts.statement: A capability sentence in README.md or docs/ is backed by a case in test/cases/ or is phrased as a target.

nodes.label: project.no-counts-in-prose@1
nodes.summary: No counts in prose

facts.statement: Prose never states a number the repository can compute; it states the command that computes it.

nodes.label: project.no-machine-paths@1
nodes.summary: Nothing this repository commits names a path of the machine it was written on

nodes.label: project.no-network-no-eval@1
nodes.summary: No network, no telemetry, no eval, no silent overwrite, no recursive deletion

nodes.label: project.no-new-nouns@1
nodes.summary: No new nouns

facts.statement: The tool gains no agents, personas, roles, tiers or registries beyond the vocabulary it has.

nodes.label: project.no-plan-stamp-without-its-event@1
nodes.summary: No plan stamp without its event

nodes.label: project.no-screen-waits-for-a-source@1
nodes.summary: A screen shows the latest reading of its sources at once, and never waits for a handler

nodes.label: project.one-derive-at-a-time@1
nodes.summary: One derive at a time per machine, and a stopped derive leaves no orphans

nodes.label: project.operation-transport-parity@1
nodes.summary: A command is the projection of a capability, or it says why it is not, and the reason is checked

facts.statement: An operation absent from the API is absent because somebody decided it, in a place that is checked; absence by nobody noticing is a defect.

nodes.label: project.optional-complexity@1
nodes.summary: Complexity is optional, not ambient

facts.statement: Keep the core closed and the edges open; a change may add sophistication behind a stable mechanism, never mandatory complexity in front of the ordinary path.

nodes.label: project.packs-carry-only-sources@1
nodes.summary: A pack that leaves the machine carries only committed sources

nodes.label: project.performance-evidence@1
nodes.summary: A performance claim carries its measurement

facts.statement: No speed-up without numbers, no budget without a run behind it, no baseline update without a reviewable diff; observed values live in the benchmark history and the baseline file, never in prose.

nodes.label: project.portable-shell@1
nodes.summary: Portable shell

facts.statement: bash 3.2 and BSD userland are the floor: no associative arrays, no mapfile, no GNU-only flags, and shellcheck -x -s bash passes on every script.

nodes.label: project.product-surface-derived@1
nodes.summary: What the product does is a catalogue object, and every public surface of it is derived

nodes.label: project.prose-states-no-version@1
nodes.summary: Prose describes the tool as it stands, without a version label

nodes.label: project.provider-support-is-declared@1
nodes.summary: What a provider's adapter can do is declared, never observed from the filesystem

nodes.label: project.providers-are-data@1
nodes.summary: What the tool knows about a provider is declared once and projected everywhere

nodes.label: project.published-evidence-is-what-ci-recorded@1
nodes.summary: A published UI shows the evidence CI recorded, never "not run" for what CI ran

nodes.label: project.reclaim-only-what-you-own@1
nodes.summary: A worker reclaims only what it owns

facts.statement: A worker removes build output only from the worktree it is working in, and never from the primary checkout or another branch's; disk pressure is reported, not resolved by taking someone else's tools.

nodes.label: project.recovery-is-idempotent@1
nodes.summary: Recovery looks before it repeats

facts.statement: Recovery resumes from the last deterministic state a worker can establish, never from the assumption that nothing happened; work is not retried until it has been shown not to have succeeded.

nodes.label: project.release-is-a-projection@2
nodes.summary: The changelog is composed, and the version is authored once

nodes.label: project.review-is-recorded-not-claimed@1
nodes.summary: Independent review is a recorded fact, weighed by evidence, never claimed and never counted

facts.statement: Gather evidence before asking, record every exchange, settle disagreement with evidence, weigh every answer received, and let the writer compute who reviewed a decision.

nodes.label: project.rule-is-a-doctrine@1
nodes.summary: A new enforced rule is a doctrine, not an inline check

facts.statement: A rule the tool enforces declares an x-majordomus block — a validator named mj_validate_<name> when a command runs it, the tests that prove it when a gate does; no command selects checks by hand.

nodes.label: project.rust-benchmark-coverage@1
nodes.summary: No endpoint of the Rust executable without a benchmark, and no number without evidence

nodes.label: project.rust-canonical-declaration@1
nodes.summary: One canonical declaration; modules compose capabilities; the root composes modules

nodes.label: project.rust-cli-evidence@1
nodes.summary: The Rust executable carries its evidence with it

nodes.label: project.rust-command-tested-in-file@1
nodes.summary: A command asserts in the file that declares it that it is what it claims, and is composed rather than registered

nodes.label: project.rust-hot-path@1
nodes.summary: A request never rebuilds canonical state, and a cache is never trusted without an equivalence test

nodes.label: project.rust-public-api-quality@1
nodes.summary: Every exported Rust item explains itself, shows itself running, and is exercised by something

nodes.label: project.scope-is-declared@1
nodes.summary: What a worker reads is declared once, and nothing outside it is read or served

nodes.label: project.session-continuity-is-portable@1
nodes.summary: Session continuity is portable, and what is portable is checked

nodes.label: project.shared-server-resilience@1
nodes.summary: Nothing a client leaves behind locks another client out

nodes.label: project.skills-are-proven-capabilities@1
nodes.summary: A skill is a capability only when something proves it

nodes.label: project.ssh-key-access-is-preauthorized@1
nodes.summary: Owner-authorized SSH access persists across clients

nodes.label: project.tests-run-in-disposable-repos@1
nodes.summary: Tests run in disposable repositories

facts.statement: Behavioural cases run through bash test/run.sh in a temporary repository each, never against this checkout.

nodes.label: project.the-briefing-is-checked-against-git@1
nodes.summary: The briefing an episode opened with is compared against git before it is believed

nodes.label: project.the-cooperation-model-is-the-owners-word@2
nodes.summary: Work moves through seats held as mesh claims, a worker lands its own green head, and every checkout is kept current

nodes.label: project.the-crate-reference-is-published@1
nodes.summary: Generated reference documentation is part of documentation closure, from its source to its public URL

nodes.label: project.the-handbook-is-built-from-the-tree@1
nodes.summary: The handbook is built from the tree it describes, and a chapter names what it rests on

nodes.label: project.the-lease-is-read-once@1
nodes.summary: The shared server's lease has one reader

facts.statement: The lease is read by `lease::LeaseFile::read` and by nothing else; a caller that needs to know where a server is asks the executable, and never the file.

nodes.label: project.the-projection-is-applied-at-landing@2
nodes.summary: A landing that changes what GitHub shows applies the change itself

nodes.label: project.the-published-ui-is-the-trunks@1
nodes.summary: The UI the site publishes is the trunk's, and a UI that is missing, older or cut short without saying so is a failed publication

nodes.label: project.the-server-sees-the-current-tree@1
nodes.summary: A long-lived process serves the repository as it is, never as it was when it started

nodes.label: project.the-session-context-is-derived@1
nodes.summary: A working context is derived, not stored

nodes.label: project.the-site-is-offered-in-every-language@1
nodes.summary: Every page of the site is offered in every declared language, derived from the English and held to it in a browser

nodes.label: project.the-site-offers-the-release-it-published@1
nodes.summary: The site offers the release that was published, on every surface at once

nodes.label: project.the-ui-wears-the-sites-navbar@1
nodes.summary: majordomus.dev is the reference for how the product looks, and every page of the UI and the Cockpit wears the site's own navbar

nodes.label: project.the-version-is-measured@2
nodes.summary: The version is measured against the public surface, not claimed

nodes.label: project.ui-conformance@1
nodes.summary: Every page of every web surface is audited, and the audit names no page

nodes.label: project.ui-derived-state@1
nodes.summary: An interface shows only what is derived, and unknown is never drawn as healthy

nodes.label: project.unknown-keys-are-errors@1
nodes.summary: Unknown configuration keys are errors

facts.statement: Every configuration file rejects a key nothing reads, and every state field is both written and read.

nodes.label: project.use-case-evidence@1
nodes.summary: A use case is proved by execution, and a capability is covered by a use case

nodes.label: project.web-surface-declared-once@1
nodes.summary: A web surface is declared once and every web projection is derived from it

nodes.label: project.web-surface-topology@1
nodes.summary: A web surface is discovered from its producer, never registered twice

nodes.label: project.why-catalogue-is-canonical@1
nodes.summary: An operational failure mode is a catalogue object, never a page

facts.statement: An operational failure mode is authored once as a catalogue object and every projection of it is derived; registering one in a projection, or writing a derived value into a source, is a defect.

nodes.label: project.work-is-claimed-before-it-is-built@1
nodes.summary: What already claims a path is checked before that path is built

nodes.label: project.work-serves-a-declared-intent@1
nodes.summary: Work serves a declared intent, and an intent is satisfied only by evidence

nodes.label: project.worktree-topology@1
nodes.summary: A branch's worktree is at <repo>-wt/<branch>, derived from git, never registered

nodes.label: project.worktrees-share-build-intermediates@1
nodes.summary: Worktrees share what cargo compiles on the way, and never the finished artifact

nodes.label: assess-before-deleting
nodes.summary: Assess before deleting

inputs: the candidates for removal, each named by its path, ref, record id or process id
a checkout with git history, the peer board and the repository's own diagnostics
outputs: a removal table naming each candidate, its class, the evidence behind the class, its risk and the action taken
a rescue ref or pushed branch for anything that held work not reachable elsewhere
the verification that ran after the removal, with its exit codes

nodes.label: deploy-site
nodes.summary: Deploy the site by hand

inputs: the commit to publish, checked out with a clean tree and contained in origin/master
zola, node_modules (npm ci) and, for the full gate, cargo; or, without cargo, the rustdoc, ui-snapshot and cockpit-snapshot artifacts of the same commit's Pages run
the operator's word, in this session, that the site is to go live now
outputs: a gh-pages commit naming the source commit, or a refusal naming the gate that stopped it
a checkpoint recording the deploy and the commit it published

nodes.label: evolve
nodes.summary: Evolve the repository's know-how

inputs: a checkout on a branch of its own, with the tool's task open and its scope naming the knowledge section
the candidates awaiting review, and whatever this session met and has not yet recorded
outputs: every reviewed candidate promoted with its evidence or rejected with its reason
for each promoted lesson that asks for one, the change to the rule, skill, document or test it belongs in
a delivered change, and an announcement and a handover that name what moved

nodes.label: implement
nodes.summary: Implement a change

inputs: the requested change, in the requester's words, with any issue or specification it names
a checkout with git history and the effective context for every path the change will touch
the repository's verification, generation and drift-check commands
outputs: the change, as coherent commits whose messages name what each proves
behavioural evidence that distinguishes the new behaviour from the old
regenerated projections and a clean drift check
an implementation record naming the invariant, the evidence, what was reconciled and what remains unsupported

nodes.label: pack-for-chatgpt
nodes.summary: Pack the sources for a ChatGPT project

inputs: a committed tree at the revision the conversation is about
the question the ChatGPT conversation is meant to answer
outputs: a verified pack directory under tmp/packs/ holding 00-INDEX.md, the shards and pack.json
the upload list, the commit, the token total and what the profile left out

nodes.label: pack-for-review
nodes.summary: Pack the repository for an outside reviewer

inputs: the question the outside review must answer, and the paths it concerns
a committed tree at the revision to be reviewed
outputs: an archive of the tracked tree at a named commit, with its file list and size
a brief for the reviewer naming the commit, the scope, the questions and what was left out

nodes.label: repo-review
nodes.summary: Repository review

inputs: a checkout of the repository with git history available
the scope under review, or the whole repository when none is given
the effective context for every path in scope (majordomus context resolve <path>)
outputs: findings, each with severity, evidence, location, the smallest correct fix and the evidence that would prove it
the list of what was checked, including the areas where nothing was found

nodes.label: report-verification-state
nodes.summary: Report by verification state

inputs: the work as it stands in the tree, with its commits and anything pushed
the commands that ran during the work, with their exit codes and the relevant output
outputs: a report whose every claim carries one of VERIFIED, PARTIAL or BLOCKED and the evidence for it
the gaps, each with the command or decision that would close it

nodes.label: adoption
nodes.summary: Getting started and adoption

facts.summary: Bringing Majordomus into a repository, new or old, without losing what people already wrote.

nodes.label: completion
nodes.summary: Completion and quality gates

facts.summary: Deciding whether work is finished, with a contract every line of which passes or fails.

nodes.label: continuity
nodes.summary: Sessions and handover

facts.summary: Stopping and resuming work across sessions and workers from durable state, never a transcript.

nodes.label: drift
nodes.summary: Drift and reconciliation

facts.summary: Detecting that policy, projections, state and git disagree, and putting them back in step.

nodes.label: extension
nodes.summary: Extension

facts.summary: Adding a kind, a rule, a command or a use case as data, with the checks that follow from it.

nodes.label: knowledge
nodes.summary: Repository knowledge

facts.summary: What the repository declares about itself: sources, nodes, edges, the plan, and searching them.

nodes.label: mcp
nodes.summary: Serving the layer to AI clients

facts.summary: One shared server per repository, every client a peer, the same layer over MCP, HTTP and the command line.

nodes.label: performance
nodes.summary: Performance

facts.summary: Benchmarks derived from the registry, baselines that are data, and budgets doctor reports against.

nodes.label: policy
nodes.summary: Policy and enforcement

facts.summary: Declaring rules, proving they are wired, and reproducing a finding.

nodes.label: workers
nodes.summary: Parallel workers

facts.summary: Several agents or people on one repository: claimed scopes, overlap, and who touched what.

nodes.label: accept-or-refuse-finished-work
nodes.summary: Decide whether finished work is actually finished

facts.summary: Evaluate a contract line by line instead of accepting a sentence that says the work is done.

nodes.label: add-a-use-case-and-prove-it
nodes.summary: Add a use case and let the tool prove it

facts.summary: Scaffold a draft for an uncovered command, validate it, run its scenario against the real tool, and see the coverage move.

nodes.label: adopt-an-existing-repository
nodes.summary: Adopt a repository that already has its own rules

facts.summary: Install the supervisory layer into a repository with a hand-written CLAUDE.md, without the tool taking ownership of a file somebody else wrote.

nodes.label: block-acceptance-on-an-open-question
nodes.summary: Block acceptance on a question nobody has answered

facts.summary: Open a question against the task, watch finish refuse completion while it is unresolved, resolve it with the answer, and only then complete.

nodes.label: capture-the-prompts-that-started-the-work
nodes.summary: Keep the prompts that started the work, below the model rather than around it

facts.summary: Wire the provider hook, prove it by running a payload through it, and see that a prompt the tool could not parse is reported rather than silently dropped.

nodes.label: carry-a-blocker-across-a-handover
nodes.summary: Hand work over with a question still open, and keep it blocking

facts.summary: Close a task into a handover while a question is unresolved, start the follow-up task, and see the same question still refuse acceptance there.

nodes.label: catch-an-agent-that-says-it-is-done
nodes.summary: Catch an agent that says it is done when it is not

facts.summary: One task, start to finish: a worker strays outside its scope, claims it is finished, hands over, and is accepted only once the repository's own verification passes.

nodes.label: checkpoint-long-work
nodes.summary: Checkpoint long work so a stop costs minutes, not the day

facts.summary: Record compact progress inside the active task at the profile interval, so a session that ends without warning leaves the next one a place to start.

nodes.label: classify-what-belongs-in-the-context
nodes.summary: Decide what belongs in the AI context, as data

facts.summary: Read the repository’s declared scope policy, see which paths are in and out of the index, and let doctor and the knowledge index apply it rather than a hardcoded list.

nodes.label: complete-an-issue-only-with-its-evidence
nodes.summary: Complete an issue only when its evidence exists

facts.summary: See an issue refuse completion while a required piece of evidence is missing, read the roadmap the milestone state derives, and keep the GitHub projection a projection.

nodes.label: deliver-issues-in-waves
nodes.summary: Deliver issues in waves the graph computes, and take the next one

facts.summary: Validate the plan, read the execution waves the dependency graph yields, see which issues are ready and which are blocked on what, and take the one issue a worker should do now.

nodes.label: document-every-directory-of-the-layer
nodes.summary: Refuse a directory of the layer that documents nothing

nodes.label: extend-what-the-executable-serves
nodes.summary: Extend what the executable serves by adding a file, never by rebuilding it

facts.summary: Add a rule, a prompt or a knowledge node to .ai/ and have it appear as an MCP resource, an HTTP route and a reference entry, with the same binary.

nodes.label: find-an-object-without-reading-everything
nodes.summary: Find an object of the layer without reading everything

facts.summary: Search durable records literally across kinds from the shell, and ask the shared server the same question over MCP with majordomus_search and majordomus_get.

nodes.label: find-out-what-drifted
nodes.summary: Find out what has drifted since anyone last looked

facts.summary: Ask what has moved, rather than whether anything is wrong.

nodes.label: follow-a-skill-the-repository-defines
nodes.summary: Follow a procedure the repository defines, and add another one

facts.summary: Read the repository's skills, take one as it is written, and add a new one by writing its file — no registry, no code, and a check that says what it examined.

nodes.label: gate-ci-on-the-tool-itself
nodes.summary: Gate CI on the tool itself, with an exit code that is a contract

facts.summary: Run the checks CI runs, read every finding with the command that reproduces it, and rely on exit codes that mean one thing each: no code means warn and continue.

nodes.label: hand-the-repository-to-a-reader
nodes.summary: Hand the repository to someone who cannot clone it

facts.summary: Take a snapshot that a model can read or a gate can run in, without sending anything untracked and without losing the file modes on the way.

nodes.label: hand-work-between-sessions
nodes.summary: Hand unfinished work to the next session

facts.summary: Stop mid-task and leave the next worker something to act on that is not a transcript.

nodes.label: install-the-tool-in-one-command
nodes.summary: Install the tool in one command, on a machine with no toolchain

facts.summary: Paste one line, get a verified binary for this machine, and run majordomus init — no git, no Rust, no Node, no Python, no root, and no way to install an archive whose digest does not match.

nodes.label: keep-decisions-out-of-the-transcript
nodes.summary: Record a decision so the next worker can find it

facts.summary: Write down what was decided and why as state, then find it again without reading a conversation.

nodes.label: keep-the-bootstrap-thin-and-within-budget
nodes.summary: Keep every provider bootstrap thin, generated and within budget

facts.summary: Regenerate AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the other provider files from one policy and prove they are stamped, point at the layer, stay under the line budget and resolve every reference.

nodes.label: keep-what-an-episode-learned
nodes.summary: Keep what an episode learned, without a model and without a conversation

facts.summary: Record a decision inside an episode, derive it into a candidate knowledge record from the ledger, read the evidence that the derivation ran, and watch a second derivation change nothing.

nodes.label: know-whether-this-work-is-finished
nodes.summary: Know whether the work in this checkout is finished

facts.summary: Ask the repository you are standing in, and be told what is still owed by name.

nodes.label: know-which-tool-is-running
nodes.summary: Check the version before trusting a diagnosis

facts.summary: Print the version every other surface derives from, and see the argument it refuses.

nodes.label: let-the-provider-draw-the-episode-boundary
nodes.summary: Have the session opened and closed without anybody remembering to

nodes.label: migrate-from-the-old-layout
nodes.summary: Move a repository from the pre-.ai layout to the layer

facts.summary: See what a migration would move, move it with a backup, and prove the result is a layer the tool reads.

nodes.label: open-and-close-a-session
nodes.summary: Record what one worker did in one sitting

facts.summary: Open a session, do the work under whatever tasks it touches, and close it into an envelope that references what it produced and copies nothing.

nodes.label: plan-a-commit-and-judge-its-message
nodes.summary: Divide a working tree into commits, and hold every message to a policy

facts.summary: Ask what this tree would commit and why, learn the scope vocabulary from the history rather than a table, and get a verdict on one message or on a whole range before a reviewer has to give one.

nodes.label: plan-the-work-as-data
nodes.summary: Keep the plan as milestones and issues the tool can validate

facts.summary: Declare milestones as outcomes and issues as execution contracts, and let the tool say what is ready and what is blocked.

nodes.label: prove-a-rule-is-enforced
nodes.summary: Prove a rule is actually enforced, not merely written down

facts.summary: Answer "is this rule real?" with a command rather than a reading of the source.

nodes.label: prove-performance-with-benchmarks
nodes.summary: Prove the tool is fast, not assume it, and refuse a regression

facts.summary: Measure every public command and every capability of the executable against a committed baseline, and let the check fail on a regression rather than a reviewer noticing later.

nodes.label: prove-what-a-task-owed-before-calling-it-done
nodes.summary: Prove what a task owed before calling it done

facts.summary: A task declares what it owes, records evidence against each obligation, and is refused when that evidence no longer describes the tree it was taken over.

nodes.label: read-back-what-happened
nodes.summary: Read back what happened, and keep the ledger within its cap

facts.summary: Read the append-only ledger as operational history, filtered by task and event, validate every line, and rotate the oldest lines into an archive rather than deleting them.

nodes.label: read-only-the-context-that-fits
nodes.summary: Read only the context that fits the budget, and know what was dropped

facts.summary: Assemble the context a worker needs now in authority order, cut it to a line budget, and see every dropped section named with its reason.

nodes.label: read-the-rules-the-tool-applies
nodes.summary: See which rules apply here and what enforces them

facts.summary: List the effective rule set, read one rule as the tool reads it, and see which of them the tool enforces and from where.

nodes.label: record-a-decision-before-it-is-forgotten
nodes.summary: Record a decision as data, and prove the tool cannot accept it for you

facts.summary: Read the decisions a repository holds, validate the whole set in one command, and watch the tool refuse to write the one status only a person may write.

nodes.label: recover-an-episode-nobody-closed
nodes.summary: Close an episode whose client never came back

facts.summary: A killed provider sends no end event. Close the episode it left open by evidence, exactly once, without claiming work it did not do.

nodes.label: resume-from-a-prompt-asset
nodes.summary: Start a session from a rendered framing, not a pasted transcript

facts.summary: List the prompt assets the repository ships, render one against the durable state, and read the context it embeds.

nodes.label: resume-in-the-right-worktree
nodes.summary: Resume in the right worktree, never against somebody else’s task

facts.summary: Find the handover that belongs to this worktree and branch, and see a task record from another checkout reported as foreign rather than enforced here.

nodes.label: run-several-workers-at-once
nodes.summary: Run several workers in one repository without them colliding

facts.summary: Give each worker a declared scope, and find out immediately when two of them claim the same paths.

nodes.label: say-what-reached-the-remote-and-what-did-not
nodes.summary: Say what reached the remote and what did not

facts.summary: The obligations that reach past the working tree are settled by asking git and the published site, so a report cannot call uncommitted work committed or unpushed work pushed.

nodes.label: say-what-the-tool-is-for
nodes.summary: Say what your work is for, once, and have every surface say it

facts.summary: Record an operational failure mode as one file and have the command line, the API, MCP and the website answer it without registering it anywhere.

nodes.label: see-what-the-repository-holds-without-reading-it
nodes.summary: See what the repository holds, and run one of its capabilities, without reading a file

facts.summary: Open the shared server in a browser and get the whole layer as pages: what exists, where each thing came from, what depends on what, what is failing, and a form that runs any capability.

nodes.label: serve-the-layer-to-ai-clients
nodes.summary: Serve the repository's AI layer to every AI client through one shared server

nodes.label: trace-a-change-to-the-context-it-affects
nodes.summary: Trace a change to the context documents it affects

facts.summary: List the scoped context documents, resolve which apply to a path and why, and find out which documents a change set touches before it lands.

nodes.label: trust-the-policy-before-reading-it
nodes.summary: Trust the policy and the profiles only after they are validated

facts.summary: Prove that the canonical policy parses with every key it needs declared, that every profile parses and the default exists, and that what the policy declares as enforced is what actually runs.

nodes.label: use-the-tool-as-your-own-in-a-shared-repository
nodes.summary: Use the tool as your own in a shared repository, and propose it to the team when it has made its case

nodes.label: work-on-a-branch-in-its-canonical-worktree
nodes.summary: Work on a branch in the one worktree it belongs to

facts.summary: Start a branch without choosing a path, find every checkout of the repository from any of them, and bring a stray one home with its uncommitted work intact.
